title_en: Nine injured in accident on the A27
description_en: On Tuesday afternoon, two vehicles collided on the A 27 motorway in the direction of Hanover. Nine people were injured, including five children. A kilometer-long traffic jam formed. At around 2:40 PM, a 35-year-old woman was driving her VW Passat on the A 27 in the direction of Hanover. Her 34-year-old husband, her one-year-old daughter, and her four-year-old son were also in the car. When a traffic jam formed behind the Vahr junction, the driver braked hard. The 47-year-old Opel driver, who was driving behind the 35-year-old woman, also hit the brakes and tried to swerve to the right but could no longer prevent a collision with the VW. Due to the collision, the VW Passat skidded, crashed into the guardrail, and was maneuvered back onto the road. The Opel driver, along with his four occupants, came to a stop on the left lane. In the accident, the 47-year-old man was seriously injured, while his 36-year-old female passenger and three children aged between six and 15 years sustained minor injuries. The occupants of the VW Passat also sustained minor injuries. Emergency services took all involved to a hospital for further treatment. Both vehicles had to be towed away. Furthermore, the Opel lost fluids. For the duration of the recovery and clean-up work, the A 27 had to be completely closed for approximately two hours. As a result, a traffic jam approximately six kilometers long formed. The total damage amounted to approximately 18,000 Euros. Investigations are ongoing.

title_en: Drunk driver causes serious traffic accident
description_en: A 49-year-old driver caused a traffic accident on Saturday evening under the influence of alcohol on the Überseestadt motorway feeder road. Three people were injured, two of them seriously. The 49-year-old was driving his BMW on the motorway feeder road in the direction of motorway 27. On the flyover, he suddenly lost control of the vehicle, skidded, and crashed into the right guardrail. Due to the impact, the car was thrown onto the opposite lane and collided there with two oncoming small vans, laterally and head-on. Emergency and police forces called to the scene found a field of debris. Vehicle parts were scattered everywhere on the road, and operating fluids were leaking from the partly heavily damaged accident vehicles. Bystanders were already helping the injured at the scene. The 49-year-old was still in the car. He was initially barely responsive and had sustained a severe hand injury. Furthermore, he was under the influence of alcohol; a breathalyzer test showed a value of 2.5 per mille. After initial treatment by paramedics, he had to be taken to a clinic. There, an ordered blood sample was taken. The 56 and 58-year-old drivers of the two Sprinter vans also sustained injuries in the accident. The 56-year-old had to receive intensive care in a hospital. The vehicles were no longer roadworthy and had to be towed away. The accident site was closed for two hours for the duration of the accident investigation and road cleaning. Investigations were initiated against the 49-year-old for driving under the influence and negligent bodily harm. His driver's license was confiscated in preparation for its revocation.

title_en: Under the influence of drugs and without a driver's license
description_en: Bremen police stopped a 43-year-old driver on Wednesday in the Neustadt district who was under the influence of drugs and did not possess a driver's license. The 43-year-old evaded a traffic stop that afternoon in the Südervorstadt district. Earlier, in Kornstraße, he had taken the right of way from a patrol car crew. Despite several stop signals, the Audi driver did not stop but sped, partially in oncoming traffic, further through the Neustadt district to Woltmershausen. In doing so, the 43-year-old almost caused two accidents. With the help of additional forces, the Audi was finally stopped in Woltmershauser Straße. The driver was handcuffed. A positive test then confirmed the suspicion: The 43-year-old was under the influence of cocaine. He was taken to the police station for a blood test. Charges were filed against him for driving a motor vehicle without a license and under the influence of intoxicating substances. Further investigations are ongoing.

On Tuesday and Wednesday, gangs of thieves were operating in Bremen-Vahr and Bremen-Osterholz. Thanks to vigilant witnesses in both cases, emergency services were able to arrest the suspected perpetrators. Around 4:45 PM on Tuesday, an 85-year-old woman was on Gustav-Radbruch-Straße with her shopping trolley. There is a bus stop there, where many people were present at the time. The senior citizen did not notice a pickpocket trio, consisting of two women and one man, approaching her. One of the three reached into her trolley and stole a wallet and a debit card.

A 13-year-old girl, who was also standing at the bus stop, observed the incident. She informed her 50-year-old father, who confronted the gang trio about the act. Thereupon, the suspected thieves fled. The 50-year-old and another witness pursued the three and alerted the police. While one of the female thieves threw the wallet to the ground, the man of the pickpocket trio managed to escape. Arriving emergency services provisionally arrested the two women. At the police station, they were fingerprinted and processed. The emergency services returned the stolen wallet and debit card to the senior citizen. The police are investigating the trio for gang theft.

Another case occurred Wednesday noon, this time in a DIY store on Werner-Steenken-Straße. Around 11:40 AM, three women and two men entered the specialized shop and stole several DIY tools, such as drills and jigsaws. They did not notice a store detective observing their act. The suspected thieves bypassed the checkout with the merchandise and stowed the stolen goods in a white Mercedes, with which they then attempted to flee.

The detective drove after them and called 110. Police officers stopped the Mercedes at the height of Osterholzer Heerstraße, shortly before the A 27 junction. The emergency services confiscated the car and had it towed away. In addition to the stolen goods from the DIY store, aquarium and baby items were found in the vehicle. The suspected thieves were provisionally arrested and fingerprinted and processed. They are being investigated for gang theft.

In both cases, the police praise the exemplary behavior of the witnesses. They followed the perpetrators at a safe distance and dialed the police emergency number. As a result, the deployed officers were quickly on site and were able to apprehend the perpetrators within a short time.

title_en: No good night for burglars in Bremen
description_en:
On Monday night, burglars broke into an ice cream parlor and a restaurant in Bremen-Mitte. A short while later, in Gröpelingen, a suspect attempted to break into several houses. In all cases, the handcuffs quickly clicked.

The operator of the ice cream parlor on Balgebrückstraße received a burglar alarm on his mobile phone around 1:20 AM on Sunday night. He could see a man in front of the terrace window. The alerted emergency forces were able to apprehend the intruder still near the crime scene. In the immediate vicinity, traces of attempted burglary were found on another house entrance door. The 25-year-old suspect has previously appeared multiple times in connection with similar offenses. He was arrested.

Just 20 minutes later, a burglar was caught red-handed in a burger restaurant on Parkallee. Residents had previously heard loud noises and alerted the police. The intruder had gained entry via a patio door and hidden from the emergency forces inside the premises. The handcuffs also clicked for the 35-year-old.

In Gröpelingen, a burglar attempted to pry open the entrance doors of at least four multi-family houses on Seewenjestraße. After a break-in into a cellar, he left the house and tried to flee through the backyard. Residents called the police via the emergency number, and the suspect was apprehended by alerted emergency forces. Shortly before, the 29-year-old threw away break-in tools such as screwdrivers and chisels.

Bremen police officers apprehended a 28-year-old man in the Östliche Vorstadt district on the night from Saturday to Sunday. He is suspected of having previously broken into the underground car park of an apartment building and, among other things, stolen money, papers, and other items from cars.

Around 3:30 AM, residents alerted the police via emergency call after hearing suspicious noises and observing people in the underground car park of the building on Hermine-Berthold-Straße. At the scene, officers encountered the 28-year-old inside the building, who initially attempted to flee. The officers stopped him and brought him to the ground. They found on him cash, a wallet, vehicle documents, and other items that originated from cars in the underground car park. Pry marks were found on several doors of the building, and corresponding burglary tools, such as screwdrivers, were seized. The 28-year-old man was taken to the police station for further measures. The criminal police have taken over the investigations, including into a possible second perpetrator.

On Wednesday, altercations occurred in Walle and Vegesack, in which knives were also used. A 60-year-old Bremen resident sustained stab and cut wounds. Emergency services provisionally arrested a total of three suspects.

On Wednesday, a confrontation occurred in Utbremen between a 36-year-old and two men aged 24 and 26. Both parties have been feuding for some time and met by chance in Landwehrstraße in the morning. An altercation immediately ensued, with the 24 and 26-year-olds punching the older man. Finally, both attackers drew a knife, and one attacked his opponent with it. The 36-year-old managed to evade the knife attack and escape into a supermarket, where he threw glass bottles at his pursuers. Alerted emergency services ended the scenario and arrested the duo. The 36-year-old had to be taken to a hospital with head injuries. Police officers found a knife with the suspects and secured it. The police secured further evidence, interviewed initial witnesses, and finally conducted threat assessments.

Around 8:45 PM, the police had to respond again to an incident involving a knife in Vegesack. There, two drunk neighbors had gotten into a dispute in an apartment building on Friedrich-Klippert-Straße. A 53-year-old punched and kicked the apartment door of a 60-year-old resident and threatened to kill him. When the latter opened the door, the attacker immediately attacked him with a kitchen knife, injuring him in the abdomen. The 60-year-old defended himself and brought his younger adversary to the ground, during which the latter lost the knife from his hand. In the subsequent scuffle, the two opponents punched each other. Alerted emergency services found both men still in the hallway. The 60-year-old had sustained further knife injuries due to his defensive movements, which were treated on site by an emergency doctor. The 53-year-old sustained a laceration to the head and had to be treated in a hospital. He was subsequently admitted to a psychiatric facility.

In both cases, the police are investigating for grievous bodily harm.

On Monday evening, altercations occurred between two youth groups in Überseestadt. Around 30 adolescents clashed at a bus stop near a sports garden and subsequently got into a fight. Pepper spray and a knife are also said to have been used. The police responded with ten patrol cars and brought the situation under control. The police were called to the Konsul-Smidt-Straße bus stop via the emergency number. Witnesses had observed a fight between two youth groups there. They are said to have fought each other after a prior verbal altercation, and pepper spray is also said to have been deployed. Upon the arrival of alerted emergency forces, all parties initially fled. Three 15-year-olds were found a short time later. They had evidently suffered eye irritations due to the pepper spray attack. One of the 15-year-olds stated that he had also been hit on the head with a knife. The trio received initial medical treatment from paramedics on site. Two of them had to be taken to a children's hospital for outpatient treatment. They were subsequently handed over to the care of their parents. A suspected perpetrator group was located near the crime scene during search operations. They initially fled upon seeing the police but were apprehended with the help of support forces. Two suspects, aged 16 and 17, were provisionally arrested and presented at a police station. After the conclusion of police measures, they were picked up by their parents. The parties involved were generally uncooperative with the emergency services. Criminal charges were filed for breach of the peace and grievous bodily harm. The criminal police are investigating. Witnesses are being questioned, and traces and evidence are being secured and evaluated. Bremen police will also increase their presence in this area and conduct controls as occasion demands.

In Bremen's Neustadt district, two acts of violence occurred on Tuesday targeting a 22-year-old and a 24-year-old man. Police have launched an investigation. Initially, the two young men were outside, near their apartment, at the corner of Große Johannisstraße and Süderstraße. Suddenly, an acquaintance joined them there, who belongs to a group currently staying overnight with the two young men. This person suddenly struck the 24-year-old man from above with a machete, while the victim tried to protect himself with his arms and hands. The 24-year-old suffered severe hand injuries, including two severed fingers. He was taken to a hospital for further treatment. The attacker fled before the arrival of the police. During a subsequent police operation at the apartment of the 22- and 24-year-old, to which officers had been called due to another altercation, the machete was recovered in connection with the incident. There, police were able to apprehend several suspects from Algeria and Morocco on site and, among other things, confiscate their mobile phones. One of the apprehended individuals subsequently became the focus of the investigation regarding the machete attack. Later, the machete was found by acquaintances of the 24-year-old in a hiding place within the apartment and handed over to the police.

title_en: Special Commission obtains further arrest warrants
description_en:
The special commission "Young Robbers" of the Bremen police arrested another four perpetrators this weekend and, together with the Bremen public prosecutor's office, obtained further arrest warrants. On Friday evening, investigators initially arrested a 19-year-old man from Morocco. He is, among other things, under urgent suspicion of having stolen a traveler's wallet in mid-November using the so-called "dance trick" (Antanztrick). With the help of video surveillance at the main train station, the thief could be identified. Another 17-year-old Albanian could also be located and arrested. He is accused of several street robberies in September and October.

In the night from Saturday to Sunday, plainclothes officers of the special commission observed two 17 and 21-year-old Algerians, who were known to the investigators from previous operations. The duo entered a snack bar on Vor dem Steintor street and ordered something to eat. Meanwhile, the younger one tried to steal from a woman by sitting with his back to her and reaching into her jacket pocket. The owner of the snack bar saw this and confronted him. Suddenly, the duo jumped up and fled without paying for the food. The owner and other witnesses ran after them and were able to apprehend one of the two. He sprayed pepper spray and initially ran off, but was apprehended just a few minutes later along with his accomplice by the responding officers.

All four individuals are in custody; further investigations are ongoing.

The special commission, consisting of experienced criminal police officers, plainclothes and uniformed officers, was specifically established to combat robbery offenses and street crime. The intensive cooperation led to the successful operations. The reason for these measures was the rapidly increasing number of robbery cases in Mitte and the Viertel district. The Bremen police had already taken a variety of intensified measures this year to reduce general street crime. These included, among other things, increased presence in public places and hotspots. However, the high number of cases prompted the establishment of a special commission that primarily focuses on combating robberies.

Plainclothes officers and task forces from the police and federal police apprehended five juveniles and young adults aged 16 to 18 in Steintor on Wednesday evening. They had previously stolen a gold chain from a 40-year-old using the "dancing trick"*.

Already around 7:10 PM, a group of six juveniles and young adults had caught the attention of federal police plainclothes investigators at the main train station. Some of them were known to the officers from previous deployments due to property offenses. They informed Bremen police task forces and followed them to the Steintor district. In front of a restaurant on the street "Vor dem Steintor", the group encountered the 40-year-old. Immediately, they surrounded him and tried to rob him using the "dancing trick". When the man resisted, a scuffle ensued, during which a 17-year-old ripped a gold chain from his neck. The plainclothes officers and task forces immediately intervened and apprehended five of the perpetrators. The foreigners from Morocco and Algeria, some of whom were minors, were taken to the police station, their identities were established, and a report for robbery was filed. A subsequent remand hearing for the 17-year-old was unsuccessful.

The police advise: Watch your valuables! Store valuables in lockable inner pockets and do not carry your cell phone or wallet loosely in your trouser pocket. Only carry as much cash as you actually need. Do not show your cell phone to strangers. Asking for the time could be a trick to prepare for a theft or robbery. Further behavioral tips can be found at www.polizei.bremen.de.

*The "dancing trick" (Antanztrick) is a form of distraction theft: The pickpocket exuberantly greets the victim, high-fives them, and puts their arm around them to dance with them, or places their leg between the victim's to show them a soccer trick. The pickpocket or an accomplice uses this distraction to steal valuables. Perpetrators have an easy time with intoxicated individuals.

title_en: Suspected perpetrator apprehended after pharmacy robbery
description_en:
An initially unknown perpetrator robbed a pharmacy in Hemelingen on Saturday lunchtime. He threatened an employee with a knife, stole cash, and fled. Emergency services apprehended a 25-year-old suspect nearby and provisionally arrested him.
At approximately 12:20 PM, the man entered the pharmacy on Hastedter Heerstraße with a knife in his hand and demanded the 34-year-old employee open the till. The woman complied, and the man grabbed cash and fled. Immediately initiated search efforts were successful: Based on the perpetrator's description, emergency services shortly thereafter apprehended a 25-year-old man nearby. He had several crumpled banknotes in his pockets. They provisionally arrested him. A remand hearing is ongoing.

Bremen police officers stopped three 20-year-old young adults in the city center early Friday morning. They are suspected of having defaced several house walls and facades with graffiti slogans. At approximately 11:40 PM, fresh defacement and three fleeing perpetrators were reported to police officers in the Old Town. At the scene, they found a large number of walls completely covered in spray paint. The initially unknown perpetrators had, among other things, sprayed "161", "Stop Capitalism" and "FCK NZS" onto house walls and facades. Witnesses had observed three men. In the street Zweite Schlachtpforte, the police officers apprehended three 20-year-olds who matched the description. They recorded their personal details; the State Security Department has launched investigations against the trio. Illegal graffiti constitutes criminal damage and is criminally prosecuted. In addition, sprayers receive the bill from the aggrieved parties. For this, they can obtain an enforcement order from the court – and that has a term of 30 years! That means that one is obligated to pay for the damage for 30 years if one possesses no money at the time of the offense.

Emergency services apprehended two men aged 34 and 39 in the Östliche Vorstadt on Friday evening. Witnesses had previously observed them defacing a house wall with graffiti.

Around 10:10 PM, police were called to Humboldtstraße because witnesses had observed two men defacing a house wall. On site, emergency services apprehended the two 34 and 39-year-old sprayers. They had spray cans with them, and there were paint residues on their clothes. Large graffiti spanning several meters was found on the facade. The owner was notified by the police and filed a criminal complaint. The two men were taken to the police station for identification procedures. The emergency services filed a criminal report for property damage. Further investigations are ongoing.

The police point out that graffiti spraying can be costly: monetary fines or even prison sentences are threatened. Furthermore, sprayers become liable for damages: For example, someone caught illegally spraying at the age of 16 risks being held responsible for the damage they caused until their 46th birthday. This is because the civil law claims of the injured party against the perpetrator are valid for that long. If only a single perpetrator from a group of sprayers is identified, they are also liable for the entire damage.

title_en: Colored slogans at schools in Horn-Lehe
description_en: Between Monday and Tuesday, two schools in Horn-Lehe were vandalized with paint. The police are looking for witnesses. Unknown individuals sprayed politically motivated slogans, such as "FCK AfD", as well as anti-police slogans, with red and black paint onto the sports hall of the Gymnasium am Vorkampsweg. The caretaker discovered the graffiti on Tuesday morning and alerted the police. Also on Tuesday morning, black graffiti was discovered at the primary school on Horner Heerstraße. Here, too, unknown individuals had sprayed, among other things, "FCK AfD" onto an exterior facade. The criminal police have launched an investigation.

Bremen Police carried out extensive measures to combat drug trafficking around the main train station and in Bremen's Viertel district from Friday afternoon until late in the evening. Drugs and cash were seized, suspected dealers were apprehended, and subsequently, apartments were searched. In addition, emergency services in the city center, Steintor, and Neustadt, together with the public order office, customs, tax authorities, and food inspection, checked kiosks, snack bars, and bars, and found some serious deficiencies.
From approximately 3:00 PM, the emergency services conducted overt and covert operations in the train station district and Steintor. During the extensive checks, several drug deals were stopped, criminal charges were filed, narcotics and cash were seized, and street dealers were apprehended. Police dogs deployed sniffed out drug stashes with cannabis, cocaine, and ecstasy in the Viertel. Furthermore, the police issued various exclusion orders.
In the eastern suburbs (Östliche Vorstadt), city center, and Neustadt, a total of thirteen establishments were the focus of emergency services in the evening. Here, various, partly serious, violations were found, such as significant hygiene deficiencies, including spoiled food, illegal employment, illegal gambling, violations of the Weapons Act, labeling requirements, and the Packaging Act, as well as cash register irregularities. Nitrous oxide was seized in one kiosk, and prescription medication in another business. Corresponding charges were filed.
For many weeks and months, Bremen Police has been increasingly committed to combating street crime and will continue these efforts together with other security authorities.

Bremen Police carried out extensive measures from Wednesday afternoon into the night to combat drug trafficking around the main train station and in the Bremen Viertel. Drugs and cash were seized in the process. Additionally, in Steintor and Huchting, kiosks, snack bars, and bars were inspected together with the public order office, customs, tax and building authorities, and food inspection, revealing serious deficiencies. A shisha bar was closed.

From approximately 3:00 PM, the deployed forces carried out open and covert operations in the station district and Steintor. During the extensive checks, several criminal charges were filed, narcotics and cash were confiscated, and street vendors were apprehended. Further investigations into this are ongoing. Additionally, the police issued various exclusion orders. Furthermore, an outstanding arrest warrant was executed, and a reported missing juvenile was returned to their facility.

In the Östliche Vorstadt and Huchting, a total of twelve establishments were simultaneously the focus of the deployed forces from afternoon until night. Here, various, partly serious violations were discovered, such as illegal gambling, partly significant hygiene deficiencies, illegal employment, violations of the Narcotics Act, labeling requirements, and the Packaging Act, as well as cash register irregularities. Corresponding charges were filed. In a tea house on Kirchhuchtinger Landstraße, there was suspicion of drug trafficking; almost 400 grams of marijuana and several sales units of cocaine were seized here, and corresponding criminal charges were filed. A shisha bar, also on Kirchhuchtinger Landstraße, was closed due to suspicion of illegal sports betting. Furthermore, the forces found several kilograms of untaxed tobacco.

For many weeks and months, the Bremen Police have been increasingly committed to combating street crime and will continue these efforts together with other security authorities.

title_en: Police seize two kilos of cocaine - Street dealer arrested
description_en: On Sunday, plainclothes police searched an apartment in Walle. Therein, they found cocaine and cash. For several weeks, investigators had been focusing on and observing two suspects aged 21 and 27. The two brothers were arrested. The search was preceded by extensive investigations by the "Street Deal" investigation group (EG). Around 8 PM, plainclothes police arrested the brothers from Guinea in front of an apartment on Wartburgstraße; they had approximately 70 grams of cocaine and other evidence on them. During subsequent apartment searches, the police found around two kilos of cocaine, several hundred euros in cash, and evidence, such as mobile phones. Arrest warrants were issued for the two accused. Further investigations are ongoing.

title_en: Police appeal for information after gas station robbery early April
description_en: On April 9, 2021, three unknown perpetrators robbed a gas station in the Peterswerder district (See Press Release 0266). They threatened the 31-year-old employee with firearms, stole cash, and fled. The police are now searching for the perpetrators with photos. Around 10:45 PM, two of the men entered the sales room of the gas station on Osterdeich street, while another waited outside the door. They went to the sales counter and told the 31-year-old to open the till, both perpetrators holding a firearm in their hand. After one of the two had taken cash from the till, all three fled on Osterdeich street in the direction of Stader Straße. The perpetrators were described as follows: The two men in the store were both approximately 20 to 25 years old and 175 cm tall. One wore a black hooded jacket, underneath a dark sweater, and dark grey work or cargo trousers. He also wore white "NIKE" brand sneakers, black gloves, and a blue face mask. The second man was dressed in a black "Tommy Hilfiger" brand jacket, black "NIKE" brand jogging bottoms, and grey "NIKE" brand sneakers. He also wore a face mask and pulled a balaclava over his head when entering the store. He wore light-colored gloves on his hands. Furthermore, they are said to have spoken broken German. The third perpetrator was approximately 185 cm tall and dressed in black. His top had red and white stripes on the collar and sleeves. He also had pulled a balaclava over his head.

title_en: Armed robberies on discounters and kiosks
description_en: On Saturday and Sunday, a discount store and a kiosk were robbed in Neustadt and Gröpelingen. The perpetrators fled with cash, and the police are looking for witnesses. Shortly before closing time, at around 9:35 PM on Saturday, a masked man entered the supermarket on Gröpelinger Heerstraße. He climbed onto the conveyor belt of a checkout and shouted that he wanted money. He then kicked an employee several times in the back, threatened him with a knife, and demanded that he open the till. After the 22-year-old opened the till, the robber took the money and then fled. The perpetrator is described as being approximately 1.85 meters tall and slim. He wore a black balaclava, black socks, dark grey shorts, an anthracite-colored hooded jacket, black gloves, and white Nike brand shoes with a black symbol. One day later, at around 9:40 PM, two men approached a kiosk on Pappelstraße. The duo threatened an employee with a knife and a blank-firing pistol, had the till opened, and grabbed several banknotes from it. They then fled in an unknown direction. The suspects are believed to be between 20 and 30 years old and between 1.70 and 1.80 meters tall. One wore a dark cap, a black sweater with a white emblem and white stripes on the arms, jeans, dark shoes, a black shoulder bag, and a dark cloth over his face. He also had a conspicuous ring on the middle finger of his right hand. His accomplice wore a black hooded jacket, black jogging pants, dark sneakers, and a light-colored cloth over his face.

An unknown man hit the manager of a supermarket in Burglesum on Saturday evening and demanded money. The plan failed and the robber fled. At around 9:20 PM, the man entered the shopping center on Bremerhavener Heerstraße, where he initially harassed two cleaners and then gained access to the office of the 33-year-old supermarket manager. Here, the unknown man repeatedly hit the employee, lightly injuring him in the process, and demanded money. When the 33-year-old tried to press the alarm button, the robber fled without any loot. He was described as approximately 40 years old and 180 centimeters tall. At the time of the crime, the unknown man was wearing a dark cap, an orange high-visibility vest, and was dressed entirely in black underneath.

On the night from Monday to Tuesday, a car burned in Bremen-Blumenthal. The fire department extinguished the vehicle. The police are investigating for arson and are looking for witnesses.Around 02:15 AM, residents reported a burning VW Passat in the turning circle of Lüssumer Heide. The car of a 44-year-old was fully engulfed in flames upon the arrival of the police officers. The fire department extinguished the flames. The car was completely damaged. The damage is estimated at approximately 10,000 Euros.The criminal police have started investigations for arson and ask: Who made suspicious observations in the area of Lüssumer Heide around 2 AM on Tuesday?

On the night from Tuesday to Wednesday, two cars completely burned out in Neustadt; no one was injured. The police are looking for witnesses. Around 10:25 PM, a 30-year-old witness noticed that a VW Polo, parked on a car transporter in Rasingstrasse, was on fire. The flames had already partially spread to a house. He alerted the police and emergency services. Afterwards, he began to extinguish the fire, as he was traveling in a company vehicle that had a water tank loaded. He presumably prevented greater damage to the house as a result. The fire department completed the extinguishing work. No one was injured; the VW Polo was completely destroyed. At 00:45 AM, residents on Neustadtswall street heard a loud bang, saw a burning Audi, and alerted the police and fire department. The quickly arriving emergency services extinguished the fire a short time later; no one was injured here either. The Audi was also completely destroyed. The criminal police have started investigations into arson in both cases and are looking for witnesses: Who made observations in Rasingstrasse, Neustadtswall, or the immediate vicinity?

title_en: After arson attack on car: Police investigating claim of responsibility letter
description_en: After unknown persons set a car on fire on 08.08.2024 in Walle in Vegesacker Heerstraße (see also press release 477), the Bremen police have received a letter of confession. The letter was published on a left-wing extremist platform. The content is assessed as authentic. The State Security department of the Bremen Police is investigating.

On Sunday afternoon, the Bremen police accompanied a gathering of the Jewish Community of Bremen and the German-Israeli Community. Furthermore, the police had information about possible further actions on Friday and Saturday in the Bremen city area. There were no significant incidents.
On Sunday, around 2:00 PM, approximately 250 to 300 participants gathered for a rally under the motto "Solidarity with Israel" on the marketplace. The Bremen police accompanied this demonstration and protected the right to freedom of speech and assembly. There were no disturbances and no traffic obstructions. The rally ended around 3:00 PM. In the afternoon, emergency services found the slogans "Free Palestine" and "Fuck Israel" on a school building in Neustadt. The criminal police have launched an investigation.
For Saturday, the group "Extinction Rebellion" had called for nationwide blockade actions (See press release 0357). In Hemmstraße in Findorff, around 11:20 AM, two people sat down on the street and held up placards. After being prompted by emergency services, they left the roadway again. The police are currently investigating whether a violation of the Assembly Act has occurred. A little later, around 12:00 PM, a man sat down on the roadway in Eduard-Grunow-Straße and also held up a placard. The police officers asked him to leave the street, took down his personal details, and issued him a ban from the area. Here too, the police are investigating whether further violations exist. In both cases, there were no major traffic obstructions.
For Friday evening, the Bremen police had information that protests against the corona measures and the curfew could occur (See PM 0357). Emergency services were present in the Östliche Vorstadt and observed several small groups on site around 8:00 PM. The police officers took down the personal details of several individuals, issued bans from the area, and filed reports of administrative offenses due to violations of the Corona Ordinance. According to current information, no further actions occurred in the subsequent course of events.

title_en: Police presence increased on the weekend
description_en:
The Jewish Community of Bremen has registered an assembly on the market square for Sunday at short notice. A demonstration planned for Saturday on the topic "Enough is Enough - We Shape Our Future" has since been cancelled. Additionally, there is information regarding possible further actions in the city area. The police will again be deployed in increased numbers to accompany assemblies, prevent disturbances, and monitor compliance with coronavirus regulations.

The initiative "People Like You and Me" had registered an assembly for Saturday. After the public order office prohibited a procession and ordered a stationary rally on the Bürgerweide under corresponding conditions (see press information from the Senator for the Interior dated 12.05.21), the organizers cancelled the assembly today.

The Jewish Community of Bremen, together with the German-Israeli Society, has today registered a rally on the market square for Sunday, between 2 PM and 3 PM, on the topic "Solidarity with Israel". The organizers expect 50 participants. The police will accompany the demonstration and have the legal mandate to protect the right to freedom of opinion and assembly. We would like to point out once again: A peaceful, non-prohibited assembly is protected by the Basic Law. Anyone who prevents or severely disrupts such an assembly commits a criminal offense.

In addition, the group "Extinction Rebellion" has called for blockade actions nationwide on Saturday. The Bremen police also have information suggesting that possible protest actions against the coronavirus measures and curfews are planned for Friday evening. An assembly registration for this action has not yet been submitted to the public order office. The Bremen police point out that assemblies must generally be registered with the public order office in advance. The police will be deployed in increased numbers and appeal: The right to freedom of opinion and assembly does not justify criminal offenses. Even if you may not approve of the political decisions, act with reason and insight. Adhere to the measures for containing the coronavirus, even if it is difficult.

On Saturday afternoon, the police accompanied the registered rally under the motto "Bremen sticks together". In total, an estimated more than 35,000 people had gathered at the rally location and in the surrounding area. Traffic disruptions occurred.

As in other German cities, tens of thousands of people in Bremen also followed the call to assemble for the rally. From 2:30 PM onwards, initially 1,500 people at its peak set off from the Viertel district on their way to the city center. From 3:00 PM onwards, the Domshof visibly filled up, so that at its peak more than 35,000 people took part in the rally. The police diverted traffic, closed streets, and ensured a smooth process without any significant incidents. At approximately 6:25 PM, the rally organizers officially ended the rally.

title_en: School route banners are being installed - Invitation to the media
description_en: Next Thursday is the start of school and on Saturday, September 4, the enrollments of Bremen's ABC-learners will take place. Further students are changing schools and daily use public transport and the "parent taxi" in addition to their bicycles. In this context, 65 school route banners will be clearly visibly placed in public traffic areas at 60 locations in Bremen. The banners bear the inscriptions "Caution! School Starts! Consideration" and "Attention School Starts" with an additional pictogram. The kick-off events will take place next Wednesday, August 25, at around 11 a.m. at Hindenburgstraße 2 with the head of the deployment directorate of the Bremen Police, Dr. Daniel Heinke, and on Monday, August 30, at 11 a.m. at Contrescarpe 26 with Senator for the Interior Ulrich Mäurer and Police President Dirk Fasse. Media representatives are cordially invited. By placing the school route banners, drivers are to be alerted to the start of school and encouraged to behave considerately and in accordance with traffic regulations, especially in the immediate vicinity of schools. Over the next four weeks, preventive checks by the Bremen Police are planned in the form of speed measurements and checks of restraint systems. Media representatives can register directly with the Prevention Centre of the Bremen Police by email praeventionszentrum@polizei.bremen.de. Further information and publications on these topics are also available at the Prevention Centre of the Bremen Police, Am Wall 195.

On Wednesday, the popular art and culture festival Breminale will once again begin on the Osterdeich meadows. To ensure that all guests can enjoy their time carefree and safely, the Bremen police will accompany the event with uniformed and plainclothes officers. In addition, the Bremen police will once again be present this year with a contact point for all visitors on the Osterdeich, between Deichstraße and Mozartstraße. This year, the Bremen police will again deploy a video trailer on the Breminale grounds. This and other measures are intended to increase the safety of all visitors and prevent crimes. There will be highly visible signage regarding video surveillance throughout the entire event area.From Wednesday to Saturday, from 7:00 PM to 2:00 AM each day, and on Sunday starting from the morning, the Altenwall between Am Wall and Tiefer, as well as the Osterdeich between Tiefer/Am Wall and Lüneburger Straße, will be closed to individual traffic. Short-term road closures by the police due to operational measures in the vicinity of the Breminale are possible. In addition to public transport, the police recommend arriving on foot or by bike.In addition to the Bremen police, the event will also be accompanied by the public order service. A security service provided by the organizer, as well as the well-known awareness teams, will also be deployed this year.A large number of people will be present simultaneously in the publicly accessible area, which can facilitate the commission of crimes.Experience shows that pickpockets exploit crowds to steal valuables unnoticed. The police therefore recommend that all visitors carry their wallets and other valuables in closed bags close to their bodies. Only take as much cash as you need. If you find yourself in a threatening situation or are even physically assaulted, draw attention to yourself by shouting loudly. Try to directly and actively ask uninvolved persons for help. In such cases, please immediately contact the Bremen police at the Breminale or dial the emergency number 110. This also applies to suspicious observations.

title_en: The number of the day is 281
description_en: On Tuesday, the Bremen police conducted bicycle registrations in Mitte and provided information on topics such as theft protection, e-mobility, and road safety. The response exceeded all expectations; 281 people took advantage of the offer and sought advice for their bikes within a few hours. The Bremen police had already set up their pavilion in the Wallanlagen, accompanied by the first sun rays of the day, in the glistening morning dew. Shortly thereafter, the first cyclists arrived at the consultation point to have their bicycles registered. The offer was so well received that additional personnel had to be deployed. The actual registration time was extended so that all citizens could be served. Besides the great response, one thing was particularly remarkable: The police officers registered many high-quality bicycles and pedelecs, costing in the four-digit range. However, it was striking that almost all of them were predominantly fitted with only cheap locks. When temperatures rise and bikes are brought out of cellars and garages, the peak season for bicycle theft also begins. Robust U-locks or armored cable locks offer the best mechanical theft protection. When purchasing, look for "tested quality" and high-quality material, such as hardened special steel, as well as robust locking systems. Always lock up your bikes so that they cannot be carried away. Incidentally, bicycle registrations also take place during the citizens' consultation hours with the contact police officers. There will also be further day events with comprehensive consultations. Information on this and help finding a good lock can also be found at www.polizei.bremen.de.

title_en: Police warns of fake water workers
description_en:
Fake water utility workers gained entry on Monday afternoon in Bremen into the apartment of an elderly resident of Bremen in the Vahr district and stole jewelry. The police warn against the renewed appearance of these criminals.

Two alleged employees of the public utility company rang the doorbell of an 87-year-old's apartment in Wilhelm-Liebknecht-Straße at around 2:30 PM and claimed they needed to check for water damage. The Bremen resident then granted entry to the fake tradesmen. While one distracted the senior, his accomplice stole three golden pocket watches from the bedroom. The duo subsequently fled the apartment.

The thieves were described as approximately 1.65 meters tall and were dressed in dark clothing at the time of the crime; one wore work gloves. One is said to be about 20 years old and thin. He had dark, curly hair and a three-day beard. His accomplice is said to be about 40 years old and corpulent. He spoke broken German.

The police advise: Do not let strangers into your home. Only grant access to tradespeople you have ordered yourself or who have been announced by the property management. If you have doubts or feel pressured, get help from neighbors or dial the free police emergency number 110.

title_en: Police once again warns of fake water utility workers
description_en:
On Tuesday, a thief posing as a fake water utility worker gained access to the apartment of a senior citizen in Hemelingen and stole cash and jewelry. The police are looking for witnesses and offering prevention tips.

Around 12 p.m., the unknown woman rang the doorbell of an 83-year-old on Hastedter Dorfstraße, claiming she needed to check the water pressure. Once the supposed water utility worker was inside the apartment, she went with the senior citizen into the bathroom and let the water run there in her presence. Allegedly needing to go back to her car, the unknown woman briefly left the bathroom, allowing her accomplice to enter during this time. When she returned, she distracted the 83-year-old woman while the unknown accomplice stole a safe containing cash and jewelry. The duo then fled the apartment.

The trick thief is described as being between 40 and 50 years old and 1.60 to 1.65 meters tall. She is also said to have been somewhat corpulent. She had dark skin and black hair. At the time of the crime, she was wearing a dark top with a white badge, white gloves, dark pants, and black athletic shoes.

The police advise: Do not let strangers into your house or apartment. If you have doubts, ask to see an ID or ask neighbors or relatives for assistance. Only grant entry to tradespeople whom you have personally ordered or who have been announced by the property management. If you feel pressured, do not hesitate and call 110.

Wednesday afternoon, a fake water utility worker was on the loose in Findorff. Under a pretext, he gained access to the apartment of an 83-year-old. In the end, the man was missing jewelry and cash. The police are providing prevention tips and are looking for witnesses to the crime.
Around 4:00 PM, a fraudster rang the doorbell of the 83-year-old man and claimed to be a water utility worker who wanted to check the water pipes. Together they went into his bathroom. The unknown person distracted the pensioner by turning on the water taps and left the apartment unnoticed. The senior citizen later discovered that cash and jewelry were missing and called 110.
The police ask: Who made suspicious observations in Grünbergstraße on Wednesday around 4:00 PM? The unknown person could not be described more precisely.
Don't give fraudsters a chance! Bremen Police advise:

title_en: Sports coach attacked - Police are looking for witnesses
description_en:
On Friday evening, two unknown perpetrators attacked a 20-year-old youth football coach in Hastedt. They also kicked him in the head. The police are looking for witnesses.

Around 6:15 PM, the 20-year-old intended to hold a football training session for about 15 children at a sports facility on Hastedter Osterseich street. The two unknown individuals were on the field at that time and were also playing football. When the 20-year-old asked them to leave the field, they refused. The coach then called the police, whereupon the two immediately attacked him. They punched and kicked him, even when he fell to the ground. In the process, they also kicked him in the head. Afterwards, they fled in the direction of the Weser weir. The alerted emergency services called an ambulance, and the 20-year-old was taken to a hospital with injuries and treated there. Immediately initiated search efforts were unsuccessful.

The perpetrators were described as follows: They were both approximately 17 to 18 years old and about 180 cm to 185 cm tall. They were wearing black sportswear; one had a "NIKE" brand rain jacket on, and the other wore a black baseball cap.

The police ask: Who observed something unusual near the sports facility on Hastedter Osterdeich street? Who saw the incident?

Every kick to a person's head can be fatal; a few centimeters can make the difference. It regularly depends solely on chance whether life-threatening injuries are caused by the kicks. The Bremen police pursue these offenses with the utmost determination.

A group of unknown individuals attacked a 22-year-old man in Neustadt on Friday. They punched him and kicked him repeatedly in the head. Bremen Police are looking for witnesses.

The 22-year-old was at a bus stop on Friedrich-Ebert-Straße at approximately 1:15 PM, when suddenly three unknown men approached him and one of them immediately punched him in the face with his fist. Subsequently, all three repeatedly punched the man and also kicked him in the head. Only when several witnesses drew attention to themselves by honking loudly did the men flee. The 22-year-old man was treated by paramedics on site and taken to a hospital for outpatient treatment.

The perpetrators were described as follows: All three are said to be between 20 and 25 years old and approximately 1.75 to 1.85 meters tall. One of them wore a light blue tracksuit jacket, a beige cap, and loose baggy jeans. The other assailant wore a grey hoodie and light baggy jeans.

Every kick to a person's head can be fatal; a few centimeters can make the difference. It regularly depends solely on chance whether the kicks cause life-threatening injuries. Bremen Police pursue these offenses with utmost seriousness.

On Sunday evening, a 25-year-old man was attacked and injured in the district. The police are looking for witnesses.
The man told emergency services at the hospital that he was walking in Steintor between Brunnenstraße and Ziegenmarkt around 7:00 PM. There, a man approached him and attacked him without warning. When the 25-year-old defended himself, the unknown assailant reportedly also injured him with a knife. Passers-by intervened. Afterwards, he went to a hospital and alerted the police. On site, the emergency services could not make any observations and also found no witnesses. The man suffered a superficial stab wound to the face. The criminal police have launched an investigation.
The perpetrator is said to have been approximately 30 years old and 185 cm tall. He was wearing a black coat. He spoke a foreign language unknown to the 25-year-old and had black skin.

On Saturday, unknown persons broke into a residential house in Huchting and stole a safe with valuable pieces of jewelry. The police are looking for witnesses who observed anything unusual. The intruders presumably gained access to the property of the detached house on Zum Huchtinger Bahnhof street via the rear. They then smashed a basement window and entered the house this way. The burglars searched cupboards and drawers and stole a silver safe containing gold necklaces, bracelets, and bangles. The perpetrators then fled undetected. The residents noticed the burglary upon their return home in the evening and alerted the police. The police are looking for witnesses and, in this context, ask: Who made suspicious observations in the area of Zum Huchtinger Bahnhof and Deichgrafenweg streets? Who noticed suspicious persons in the vicinity? The police warn against purchasing the stolen jewelry. A potential buyer makes themselves liable to prosecution and can be prosecuted for receiving stolen goods.

Unknown burglars broke into a residential house in Horn over the weekend. The perpetrators were able to flee undetected. The police are looking for witnesses.

The intruders gained access to the property on Marcusallee via the rear garden and then entered the single-family house through a patio door. They subsequently searched the room, cupboards, and drawers. From these, the burglars took cash, wallets, a handbag, and expensive jewelry. In addition, the intruders stole a safe, which was, however, left behind in the garden before they fled undetected.

Investigators are looking for witnesses and ask: Who made suspicious observations in the night to Sunday or in the past few days at the crime scene and around Marcusallee? Has anyone noticed a suspicious vehicle?

Since mid-October, the Bremen Police have been publishing a weekly overview of current burglaries in Bremen at www.polizei.bremen.de. The map shows in which areas residential houses and apartments have been broken into. The aim of this prevention project is to raise awareness among individuals and to inform citizens where they should be particularly vigilant. Very important: In case of suspicious observations, immediately alert the police via the free emergency number 110.

An unknown man broke into a mosque in Gröpelingen on Tuesday night. In doing so, he stole cash from a donation box. On Tuesday morning, members of the congregation in Stapelfeldstraße noticed signs of a break-in and alerted the police. Surveillance camera footage shows how a man smashed a window at approximately 2:30 AM, then searched several cabinets, and finally took the donation box. He then fled in an unknown direction. The criminal police have launched an investigation.

On Tuesday evening, three unknown individuals robbed a 46-year-old man of a luxury wristwatch in the St. Magnus district. The police are looking for witnesses and warn against purchasing it. Yesterday evening, the man traveled by tram to Bremen Central Station. There, he already noticed three men who sat near him. The trio also followed him when he changed to a train heading towards Bremen-Nord. When he arrived at Lesum station around 7:50 PM and walked to his car, which was parked near a car dealership, he saw the men following him. A little later, he was put in a headlock from behind and pulled to the ground. When the 46-year-old resisted, two of the perpetrators fled in the direction of Lesum station. The third one grabbed his briefcase, which he was carrying, and ran in the opposite direction. The 46-year-old man ran after him, whereupon the unknown individual dropped the bag and also fled in the direction of Lesum station. The man sustained minor injuries from the incident and only later noticed that his valuable Rolex brand wristwatch was missing. The police warn against purchasing the stolen piece of jewelry. A potential buyer makes themselves liable to prosecution and can be prosecuted for receiving stolen goods. The three unknown individuals were described as follows: The men are all said to have been around 25 years old and 1.80 meters tall. They also shared the characteristic of having short black hair and a three-day beard. One of the perpetrators wore a black jacket, blue jeans, and black sneakers. Another was dressed in a white jacket with black appliqués, black trousers, and black trainers.

Late on Friday evening, a hitherto unknown perpetrator robbed a 54-year-old woman in Bremen's Old Town. The robber managed to escape with a luxury wristwatch. The police are looking for witnesses.

The 54-year-old was engaged in conversation by the later perpetrator in front of a hotel on Wachtstraße. Suddenly, without warning, the man ripped the valuable wristwatch from her wrist. The robber then fled in the direction of Schlachte. The woman sustained a minor injury to her wrist.

The stolen item is a silver-black women's wristwatch of the brand Omega Speedmaster. The police warn against purchasing the stolen piece of jewelry. A potential buyer makes themselves liable to prosecution and can be prosecuted for receiving stolen goods.

The robber was described as being between 1.75 to 1.85 meters tall, approximately 20 to 25 years old, and having a dark complexion. He wore a black cap, a black zippered jacket, and blue jeans. He spoke with a French accent.

On Tuesday afternoon, an unknown person robbed a 79-year-old in Bremen's Neustadt district. The perpetrator fled undetected. The police are looking for witnesses.
The 79-year-old was walking with his wife, who uses a rollator, around 1 PM along Kornstraße in the area of the Stenumer Straße bus stop. The unknown person approached the couple and tried to sell them a mobile phone. After they repeatedly refused to buy it, the man initially turned away but then approached the couple from behind and tore a gold chain from the 79-year-old's neck, causing him to stumble. The robber fled undetected in the direction of Werdersee.
The senior citizen and his wife initially called their daughter for help and, with her, unsuccessfully searched for possible escape routes of the unknown person. Afterwards, they contacted the police emergency number. Bremen police point out that after such incidents, the emergency number should be called as quickly as possible to enable an immediate search for the suspects.
The perpetrator was described as noticeably short, about 1.50 to 1.55 meters tall, slim, and approximately 25 years old. He had a dark complexion and spoke broken German. At the time of the crime, he was wearing a dark blue tracksuit jacket and black trousers.

title_en: Control Group Sanctions Violations by Speeders and Posers
description_en:
The Control Group for Speeders and Posers of the Bremen Police checked various vehicle drivers in the city area over the Easter weekend and punished many violations. The specialists checked around 30 vehicles on Good Friday and Saturday and detected several speeding violations. The most egregious offender was a driver who was traveling at 124 km/h on Kurfürstenallee instead of the permitted 50 km/h. He and five other speeders in various city districts face corresponding driving bans. In addition, the control group punished administrative offenses such as red light violations and illegal overtaking on the right. Another vehicle driver and an e-scooter rider were on the road without insurance coverage; criminal charges were filed against them accordingly. The police also conducted traffic education talks, issued defect notices, and investigated tips regarding alleged poser gatherings. In one case, a driver was prohibited from continuing their journey due to technical modifications.
In addition to traffic controls and targeted operations, the Bremen Police are once again deploying unmarked patrol cars on several days a week to combat aggressive behavior in road traffic. The control group consists of trained personnel and specifically targets speeders and posers. The specialists patrol throughout the entire Bremen city area, also taking into account complaints and tips from the public, which typically increase in summer. They are instructed to prevent and punish typical violations such as loud acceleration, unnecessary back and forth driving, harassing posing, technical manipulations of motor vehicles, brief speeding offenses, and illegal vehicle races.

title_en: The Speeders and Posers Control Group punishes violations
description_en:
Police specialists focused on speeders and 'posers' yesterday evening in the Überseestadt and penalized a total of 24 speeding violations. The worst offender was a 26-year-old, who was driving at 128 km/h instead of the permitted 50 km/h. He and three other speeders can expect corresponding driving bans and substantial fines.

Yesterday, between 5:00 PM and 8:00 PM, emergency services used measuring vehicles to conduct checks in the Kommodore-Johnsen-Boulevard area and Konsul-Smidt-Straße. There, a 23-year-old novice driver, who is still in their probationary period, passed the measuring point at 84 km/h instead of the permitted 50 km/h. He faces a substantial fine and a driving ban. The driving behavior of a pizza delivery driver was also risky. He was driving his car more than 60 km/h too fast. He must expect a substantial fine. In addition, his driving license will be confiscated for two months. A 24-year-old driving a high-powered Mercedes from a rental company was also much too fast. When he passed the measuring point, his speedometer showed 100 km/h instead of the permitted 50 km/h. Furthermore, he was not registered as a driver in the rental agreement, and the Mercedes was impounded. Additionally, he must pay a high fine and can expect a driving ban of at least one month. The worst offender was a 26-year-old, who sped through the Überseestadt at 128 kilometers per hour and was stopped by the emergency services. He also receives a fine of 680 Euros and a three-month driving ban. In total, 24 traffic violations were identified by the specialists. Educational discussions about traffic safety were held with all of them. In addition, the emergency services also penalized three violations related to 'posing'. Two drivers were prohibited from continuing their journey.

The problems in the Überseestadt with the phenomenon of speeders/'posers' are known to the Bremen police. Gerrit Becker, Head of the Traffic Police, says: "Yesterday's control measures are part of the concept for combating the speeder/'poser' problem and will be continued as appropriate to the situation."

In addition to traffic controls and targeted operations, the Bremen police repeatedly deploy unmarked patrol cars to combat aggressive behavior in road traffic. The control group consists of trained officers and specifically targets speeders and 'posers'. The specialists also take into account complaints and tips from the public, which typically increase in summer. They are instructed to prevent and penalize typical violations such as loud acceleration, aimless driving back and forth, harassing 'posing', technical manipulations of vehicles, temporary speeding, and illegal street races.

On Thursday morning, Bremen police conducted a major traffic check in the Eastern Suburb. The focus was on speed monitoring. In total, aspiring police officers and their instructors identified 170 violations. Between 8:00 AM and 11:00 AM, officers conducted speed measurements on the Osterdeich near the Weserstadion. During the mentioned period, a total of 1125 cars passed through the area, from which 170 violations were recorded. The most egregious offender was a driver who, in a 30 km/h zone, was driving 60 km/h after deducting the tolerance. Even though no driving bans were issued, the trainees issued 16 warnings, identified 18 administrative offenses, and initiated seven fine proceedings. The trainees were supported by mobile speed monitoring units and specialized traffic monitoring units.

Even in Bremen, stories of easily earned money, Bitcoins, and cryptocurrency are repeatedly luring people onto dubious online trading platforms. The victims invest, believing they have been well advised, and never see their money again. The Bremen criminal police are currently investigating several cases of online investment fraud. The police are warning against this scam and providing safety tips. Many victims are inexperienced in online trading: Cybercriminals exploit this for their schemes, transferring their victims' money to their own accounts abroad. To acquire potential victims, cybercriminals create fraudulent investment platforms for online investments on the internet. These platforms look reputable at first glance and are advertised on trustworthy websites and currently primarily on social media like Facebook. Once the interested customer has registered online with the trading platform, they are directly contacted by the cybercriminals. The "traders" are in reality fraudsters who operate from call centers. They intensively support their "customers" via phone and messenger service. The criminals, who convincingly and confidently pose as real brokers, also often use so-called remote software (AnyDesk, Teamviewer). This is used under the pretext of explaining and setting up the user account for the customers. Meanwhile, the fraudsters unnoticeably steal data, e.g., credit card and bank account information. With the access data obtained in this way, the fraudsters later transfer further amounts to themselves without the knowledge of the victims. In Bremen, such fraudsters connected to the victims' computers via remote maintenance software and enabled online banking access. During the consultation, the victims were then pressured, after an initial rather low deposit of 250 Euros, to transfer increasingly larger sums to their supposedly newly established investment accounts, for example in Austria and Latvia. The private investors could see on these accounts how their invested capital rapidly grew and, at the prompting of their "brokers," made increasingly higher deposits. In reality, at this point, the alleged financial advisors had already siphoned off their investors' money. The investment account never actually existed; no customer ever got their money. The police warn and give tips:
