title_en: Police warn: Series of shock calls
description_en:
Within a few days, there were more than a dozen shock calls throughout the city. Fraudsters repeatedly posed as fake lawyers and police officers on the phone. The warning is primarily directed at elderly people: Criminals attempted to obtain money and valuables through perfidious tricks. They put seniors under pressure and incited fear by pretending that only by paying 'ransom' would they avoid going to prison. The police are offering prevention tips.
Last weekend, fraudsters succeeded a total of three times in depriving mostly elderly people of their savings. In various districts, the criminals called pensioners and immediately put them under pressure. For example, they posed as police officers and pretended that fraudsters were going from house to house, robbing people of their belongings. In one case last Thursday, unknown individuals posed as a police officer and a public prosecutor and told a 70-year-old on the phone that she was under investigation. Only by paying a 'ransom' would the investigation be dropped. The senior then withdrew cash and valuables from her bank and deposited everything in front of a building. The criminals were able to pick it up unnoticed. The mother of the 70-year-old learned of the incident and called 110.
The police are warning about a series of shock calls: If a police officer contacts you by phone and asks for your money and valuables, and urges you to hand them over: Hang up. These are fraudsters at work! The police will never ask you for your money or valuables or request their handover. Remain suspicious and, if in doubt, ask trusted people for help. More tips and information are available at the Bremen Police Prevention Center at (0421) 362-19003 or at www.Polizei.Bremen.de.

On Saturday afternoon, a 36-year-old man is reported to have fired a shot from a blank gun from his balcony in Horn-Lehe. This triggered a major police operation.

Witnesses reported to the police around 3:50 PM a shot from a balcony of an apartment building in Kohlmannstraße. They also stated that the 36-year-old had been handling a pistol. The alerted emergency forces quickly secured the area. After the exact apartment was determined, the alleged shooter was encountered leaving the house and provisionally arrested by special forces. In his apartment, they found a blank gun and ammunition. The police have initiated further investigations due to a violation of the Weapons Act. Furthermore, the assumption of costs for the operation by the 36-year-old is being examined.

On this occasion, the police once again explicitly warn against handling blank guns and so-called imitation firearms. From a distance or in darkness, it may not always be immediately possible to recognize a fake weapon, and it can trigger a police operation. The police must take reports of such incidents very seriously and consequently, to avert danger for others and themselves, act as if the weapon were real.

title_en: Man with a gun triggers police operation
description_en:
On Monday evening, a 19-year-old was handling an airsoft pistol in the station district, triggering a police operation. Around 7:15 p.m., a witness reported via emergency call that a man was handling a firearm in the station. Alerted emergency services confronted the 19-year-old in the station square. He was secured on the ground and handcuffed. He was carrying an airsoft pistol and a machete, both of which were confiscated. The arrested person was under the influence of drugs, so the police called in a crisis intervention service. After the medical examination was completed, the police issued him a ban from the station vicinity. Investigations for violating the Weapons Act were initiated against him.

On this occasion, the police once again emphatically warn against handling imitation firearms. At a distance or in the dark, it may not always be immediately possible to recognize an imitation weapon, which can trigger a police operation. The police must take reports of such incidents very seriously and consequently act as if the weapon were real to avert danger to others and themselves.

title_en: Neighborhood dispute escalates - Man fires tear gas weapon
description_en:
On Tuesday night, neighborhood disputes arose in Woltmershausen due to excessively loud music. A 60-year-old man then shot at his neighbors with an irritant gas pistol.

Two residents, aged 23 and 50, from Roccoweg in Rablinghausen visited their neighbor several times during the evening to alert him to his loud music. When they complained again around 11:30 p.m., the 60-year-old resident suddenly fired an irritant gas pistol towards the two individuals upon opening his apartment door. They suffered eye irritation and respiratory problems.

The suspect was still found at his residential address by alerted emergency services. By order of the public prosecutor's office, a search of the apartment was carried out. During this, the irritant gas pistol used, hidden in a freezer compartment, two additional blank-firing guns, and a crossbow were found and seized.

Further investigations against him for dangerous assault are ongoing.

An unknown man robbed a 57-year-old woman of her handbag in Osterholz on Thursday afternoon. The police are looking for witnesses. At approximately 3:15 PM, the woman turned with her bicycle from Ehlersdamm street into a path towards Hans-Bredow-Straße and rode parallel to the tram tracks there, when the man approached her from behind on a bicycle. As he rode next to her, he tried to snatch her handbag from the bicycle basket, thereby pulling the woman down, as she had fastened the strap to the saddle. The 57-year-old fell, the man cut the strap with a knife and fled on his bicycle down a side path towards Langwedeler Straße. The woman was slightly injured by the fall but declined an ambulance. Immediately initiated search operations were unsuccessful. The woman was able to find her bag a short time later on a garage yard in Völkerser Straße by tracking her mobile phone. However, cash and bank cards were missing. The perpetrator was described as follows: He is said to have been approximately 180 cm tall and slender. He was dressed in black and had pulled a black tubular scarf over his face; he also wore a black hood. He is believed to have been riding a black mountain bike.

On Friday, robberies occurred in Obervieland and Neustadt. A 75-year-old woman had to be treated in a hospital. The police are looking for witnesses.

Around 8 PM, a 92-year-old man was traveling on bus line 26 towards Überseestadt, got off at the Gottfried-Menken-Straße stop in Neustadt, and walked towards Hinrich-Fehrs-Straße. Suddenly, he noticed a man approaching him from behind and speaking to him. Shortly after, the man grabbed the senior citizen and put his leg in front of the 92-year-old's legs. After that, the unknown assailant ran away. The senior then noticed that his wallet was missing. The perpetrator is described as 1.90 meters tall and strongly built. He is believed to be around 25 years old and was wearing a black parka with a button placket on the collar and a black cap.

Around 4:35 PM, a 75-year-old woman was returning from shopping on Kattenturmer Heerstraße when, in the supermarket parking lot, an unknown person suddenly snatched her handbag from behind. The senior citizen fell to the ground and was injured in the process. The perpetrator fled in an unknown direction. On site, the woman received medical attention from paramedics and was taken to a hospital for further treatment. Several witnesses described the perpetrator as follows: He is believed to be between 16 and 17 years old and has a dark complexion. He was wearing a dark sweater with a black jacket over it, dark grey sweatpants, and black sneakers.

On Thursday, robberies occurred in the districts of Osterholz and Obervieland. In one case, a 77-year-old woman was locked in a storage room. A 13-year-old boy was threatened with a knife. The police are looking for witnesses.

A 77-year-old woman was going into her apartment on Tessiner Straße around 12:15 PM when an unknown man spoke to her. He pretended to be a police officer and told her that someone had tried to break into her home and that he needed to take her valuables for safekeeping. The senior citizen granted him access to the apartment and handed over money and jewelry. The alleged police officer then locked the 77-year-old woman in a storage room and fled. Neighbors heard cries for help and then alerted the emergency services.

The perpetrator was described as follows: He is said to be between 1.80 and 1.90 meters tall and 25 to 35 years old. He has dark blonde hair, was dressed in black, and was of slender build. He also wore a patch with an unknown motif on his arm.

A few hours later, a robbery occurred on Morsumer Straße in the Kattenesch district. A 13-year-old boy was on his way home around 6:15 PM when an unknown person called out to him. When the 13-year-old stopped, the person pulled out a one-handed knife and demanded his jacket. The 13-year-old handed it over. The perpetrator then asked for cash and patted down the jacket. When he found nothing, the 13-year-old fled home and then alerted the police.

title_en: Defusal of a World War bomb
description_en: In Huchting, a 250-kilogram World War bomb was found during exploratory work. This will be defused in the course of Wednesday afternoon. For this purpose, evacuations are necessary within a 300-meter radius around the discovery site. The American aerial bomb was found at the discovery site in Willakedamm street by experts from the Bremen police's ordnance disposal unit. Demolition expert Hans Mohr is expected to defuse the bomb on Wednesday, November 27, 2024, starting at 2 PM. Evacuation measures will begin at 10 AM. All buildings in the immediate vicinity of the discovery site, the "inner circle" (300 meters), must be evacuated. For this, all persons must leave their residential and business premises from 10:00 AM. In the "outer circle" (500 meters) around the discovery site, no people are allowed to be outside buildings during the defusal. During the defusal, residents should avoid proximity to windows and stay in parts of buildings that are facing away from the bomb. Tilt your windows. Please refer to the published map attached to this message to determine whether you are in the inner or outer circle. Kirchhuchtinger Landstraße is affected by the measures in any case. For this reason, there will also be restrictions and cancellations for buses and trams from 10:00 AM. The police recommend avoiding the area over a wide range. Schools, kindergartens, and care facilities are all affected by the measures. These will be informed by their operators and competent authorities about any closures or restrictions. Residents can stay at the "Roland zu Bremen" school on Flämische Straße for the duration of the measures.

title_en: Suspected two aerial bombs in Farge - Evacuation on Sunday
description_en:
During exploratory work at the former Farge tank farm, two suspicious objects were discovered, which are very likely two unexploded bombs from the Second World War. Defusal is planned for next Sunday, April 26. All residents within the evacuation radius must leave their homes by 8 AM. The presumably British aerial bombs, each weighing 500 kilograms, are located approximately 450 meters away in the wooded area of the former Farge tank farm. The bomb disposal experts from the Bremen Police Explosive Ordnance Disposal Service, Thomas Richter and Hans Mohr, plan to defuse them around 1 PM on Sunday afternoon. This is expected to last until late afternoon. Should defusal not be possible, the bombs will be detonated in a controlled manner. A drone will be used for aerial overviews. The evacuation radius is 1000 meters (see map).

All residents must leave their homes by 8 AM due to the extensive preparatory work, and thus also the evacuation area. The "In den Sandwehen" secondary school will serve as a meeting point for evacuated persons. If you cannot find accommodation with family or friends, you can stay there in the meantime. Please remember to take necessary medications and provisions with you. Please leave your windows tilted when leaving your homes. Approximately 2000 people are affected by the evacuation.

Important information for persons with reduced mobility: People who require assistance are asked to contact the Bremen Fire Department at telephone number 0421 33610-371. BSAG lines will no longer serve stops in the affected area starting at 8 AM. However, they can still pass through until noon. Train services will also be affected and temporarily suspended.

title_en: Evacuation on Sunday due to possible detonation of four unexploded bombs in Bremen-Farge
description_en:
During exploratory work on the site of the former world's largest tank farm in Farge, four suspected unexploded bombs from the Second World War were discovered. The finds are presumed to be 500 kg bombs, which could be equipped with a special fuse system that makes defusing impossible. In this case, a detonation would be unavoidable.

The final investigation of the suspected items will take place on Saturday, March 8, 2025, by the explosive ordnance disposal service of the Bremen police. Should the suspicion be confirmed, comprehensive evacuation measures will have to be carried out on Sunday, March 9, 2025. The police will issue another statement on Saturday regarding this.

Evacuation measures and schedule
The evacuation radius is 1000 meters around the discovery site.

title_en: Severe environmental violation - Water Protection Police collects security payments
description_en: During a routine inspection of a car carrier sailing under the flag of the USA in Bremerhaven, a serious violation of the provisions of the Ballast Water Management Convention was discovered. The Bremen Water Police penalized the violation and collected security deposits on Tuesday. The incident occurred on November 11, 2024, in German territorial waters off the island of Borkum. Approximately 800 tons of untreated ballast water were discharged into the North Sea from this ship. Due to this violation, the Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency ordered security deposits totaling 52,000 Euros against the responsible captain and the First Nautical Officer of the ship. These were collected today. The Ballast Water Management Convention aims to prevent the spread of invasive species, viruses, and bacteria through untreated ballast water originating from different marine areas. The discharge of untreated ballast water poses a serious ecological threat and contradicts international environmental protection regulations.

title_en: Water Police collects security payments after serious environmental violation
description_en:
During a routine inspection of a cargo ship sailing under the flag of Antigua and Barbuda in Bremerhaven, a serious violation of the regulations of the Ballast Water Management Convention was detected. The Bremen Water Police sanctioned the violation and collected security deposits on Tuesday.

The incident occurred on January 9, 2025, in German territorial waters near the islands of Borkum and Juist. Approximately 900 tons of untreated ballast water were discharged into the North Sea from this ship. Due to this violation, the Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency ordered security deposits totaling 52,000 Euros against the responsible captain and the Chief Mate of the cargo ship. These were collected on Tuesday.

The Ballast Water Management Convention aims to prevent the spread of invasive species, viruses, and bacteria through untreated ballast water originating from various marine areas. The discharge of untreated ballast water poses a serious ecological threat and is contrary to international environmental protection regulations.

title_en: Violation of Ballast Water Regulations: Security deposits against captain and officer seized
description_en: During a routine inspection of a container ship sailing under the Maltese flag, a serious violation of the Ballast Water Management Convention regulations was discovered last week in Bremerhaven. On Saturday, the Bremen Water Police also penalized an environmental violation in the Bremerhaven marina. The inspection took place on July 10, 2024, at the Stromkaje. According to the entries in the ballast water logbook, the ship had discharged approximately 900 tons of untreated ballast water into the Baltic Sea at the end of June. The incident occurred on June 26, 2024, in German sovereign territory north of the island of Rügen. Due to this violation, the Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency ordered security payments totaling 52,000 Euros against the responsible captain and the First Nautical Officer of the ship. These were collected last Friday. The Ballast Water Management Convention aims to prevent the spread of invasive species, viruses, and bacteria through untreated ballast water originating from different marine areas. The discharge of untreated ballast water poses a serious ecological threat and contradicts international environmental protection regulations. At noon on Saturday, Bremen Water Police officers registered water pollution in the form of an oil slick at the location 'Am Neuen Hafen'. To prevent further spread and contain the pollution, the German Federal Agency for Technical Relief (THW) erected an oil boom. According to witness statements, the driver of a motorboat is said to have previously poured the liquid into the water. Criminal investigations against the 76-year-old for water pollution are ongoing.

On Saturday evening, Werder Bremen and Köln faced each other at the wohninvest-Weserstadion. The police accompanied the events surrounding the sold-out match, and there were several incidents. The guest supporters arrived by tour buses, cars, and train. During the match, flares were set off in the stadium in the area of the away fans. The police filed corresponding charges for violations of the Explosives Act. After the final whistle, fans of both teams largely left the stadium in an orderly manner. Due to preventive police measures, there were no major riots or confrontations. The emergency services accompanied the individual fan groups to their meeting points. During a confrontation at the main train station involving Köln supporters, police had to use pepper spray, resulting in several people sustaining minor injuries. Overall, there were several event-typical crimes that evening, such as the robbery of a fan scarf or one or two physical altercations. In a fight between two football supporters, an uninvolved woman fell and had to be taken to the hospital. Additionally, a police officer was hit with a bottle in another situation but remained unharmed. Investigations into these incidents are ongoing. The Bremen police received support that evening from emergency forces from Lower Saxony and Hamburg, as well as the Federal Police.

On Friday evening, Werder Bremen and Bayern Munich faced each other at the wohninvest-Weserstadion. The police monitored the events surrounding the sold-out match. In the vicinity, everything was largely peaceful; however, inside the stadium, there were several incidents involving the use of pyrotechnics, in which a woman was slightly injured. The away fans predominantly traveled individually by coach and car. During the match, numerous flares were set off in the stadium in both the home and away fan sections. A female visitor sustained burns and had to receive treatment. The police filed corresponding charges for dangerous bodily harm and violations of the Explosives Act. After the final whistle, fans of both teams largely left the stadium in an orderly manner. Due to the preventive measures taken by the police, there were no major riots or confrontations. Emergency services accompanied the fan groups to their meeting points and ensured a smooth departure. Following the events from May (see also press release 471), the police were able to identify additional suspects. They were released on the spot after identification; further investigations into this matter are ongoing. Overall, that evening saw only isolated football-related offenses, such as dangerous bodily harm caused by a thrown beer cup or the theft of a fan scarf, which led to charges. Bremen police received support that evening from officers from Lower Saxony and Schleswig-Holstein, as well as federal police in the area of the main train station.

Several motorcades and numerous celebrants on the occasion of Sunday's Turkey election caused a lot of work for the Bremen police. The celebrations were predominantly peaceful; however, a multitude of traffic offenses were penalized and charges under the Explosives Act were filed.

On Sunday evening, several motorcades formed in the city, numbering about 50 vehicles at their peak. The participants celebrated the Turkish runoff election. The emergency services identified many traffic violations, such as leaning out of moving vehicles and national flags waving out. Pyrotechnics were set off. There were also reports of shots from blank-firing pistols fired from inside the cars. Additionally, up to 300 celebrants were on the streets and sidewalks. Due to the high volume of traffic and the resulting dangers for celebrants on and next to the road, Breitenweg was temporarily completely closed. Afterwards, the celebration slowly dispersed.

There were no known confrontations; the atmosphere was predominantly festive. Nevertheless: Ensuring safety, especially in road traffic, has the highest priority despite all reasons to celebrate. Joy about an event at no time justifies disregarding traffic rules and results in reports of administrative offenses.

title_en: Hate crime - Police searches apartments in Bremen
description_en:
As part of the second nationwide action day against hate postings, the Bremen police today searched the homes of two Bremen residents. The 21 and 59-year-old men are suspected of having deliberately posted hate comments on social media after a policewoman and a policeman were killed during an operation in Rhineland-Palatinate. The nationwide search measures included a group of people who are being investigated by the EG Hate Speech established at the LKA Rhineland-Palatinate. The EG Hate Speech was set up after the killing of a uniformed policewoman and a uniformed policeman near Kusel at the beginning of February, after numerous hate comments had appeared online.

During the search in Bremen, various weapons and data carriers were seized, which are now being evaluated. The legal basis for the search was a judicial order from the Bremen District Court at the request of the Bremen public prosecutor's office. The investigations by the State Protection Department of the Bremen police are ongoing. The action took place simultaneously and in coordination with parallel police measures by the LKA Rhineland-Palatinate. Nationwide searches took place since 6 am for this purpose.

Senator for Interior Ulrich Mäurer: "The networking of conspirators and enemies of the constitution in virtual space poses a very high threat potential. They spread a wave of hatred that also incites individuals to radicalize and take action. Our security authorities consistently take action against the spread of hate and incitement on the internet, before insults and threats turn into deeds. The police and justice system have once again sent a clear signal today: Anyone who incites and threatens must expect charges and convictions."

Bremen police also participated on Thursday in the 10th nationwide action day against hate postings and visited the apartment of a Bremen resident. The man is suspected of having authored hate postings on social media. Last year, the man wrote under a politician's post, "Alles für Deutschland!!! Aber so was von." This morning, investigators visited his apartment to hold a police warning interview. Further police measures and investigations for using symbols of unconstitutional organizations are ongoing.

The number of hate posting cases recorded by the police has risen sharply nationwide last year. In total, the number of cases more than doubled from 3396 to 8011. One reason for this increase is, among others, the BKA's Central Reporting Office for Criminal Content on the Internet (ZMI BKA), which, in cooperation with its partners, is increasingly shedding light on the dark figure in the internet. Also in the run-up to today's action day, a significant proportion of hate postings were processed there again and forwarded to the law enforcement authorities in the federal states. Hate and incitement on the internet are breeding grounds for radicalization and drivers of violent acts.

Calls to commit crimes, threats, coercion, or incitement to hatred on the internet are criminal offenses that can be punished with up to five years imprisonment. If you come across hate postings online or are a victim yourself, you should report it to the police. Report hate postings to social network providers and urge them to delete criminal content!

On Wednesday afternoon, a drunken man repeatedly displayed the Hitler salute in the Neustadt district. The police apprehended a 38-year-old suspect.

Customs officers had called the police at midday because a drunken man was walking along the ramp to Oldenburger Straße. On the Stephanibridge, they caught up with the man to guide him away from the busy federal road. There he repeatedly displayed the Hitler salute to the customs officers and behaved aggressively. He repeatedly attempted to continue his path on the road towards the city center. Fortunately, no one was harmed in the process. The alerted patrol car crew apprehended the suspect and took him to the station, where he spent the next few hours in police custody.

A report was filed against the 38-year-old for using symbols of unconstitutional organizations. The investigations are ongoing.

Unknown persons blew up a cigarette machine in Kattenturm on Tuesday night/Wednesday morning. The police are looking for witnesses and warning.

At 01:15 AM, residents in Anna-Stiegler-Straße heard a loud bang. When they looked onto the street, they saw a smoke cloud and two people, one of them wearing a leather jacket and cap, tampering with a cigarette machine. Subsequently, the persons fled into a dead-end path. The perpetrators had blown up the cigarette machine using illegal firecrackers and stolen cigarette packs and cash. Due to the explosion, the machine was almost completely destroyed. Bremen Police are now investigating for causing an explosive detonation.

The police strongly warn: Anyone who uses illegal firecrackers or makes them themselves puts themselves and others in great danger. Because with homemade fireworks, even minimal thermal or mechanical influences can under certain circumstances lead to an explosion. Blast trauma, burns, mangled or severed body parts, and other serious injuries, up to and including death – these can be the consequences of improper use of illegal, homemade firecrackers.

Unknown individuals blew up a cigarette machine in Gröpelingen on the night from Wednesday to Thursday, causing property damage. The police are looking for witnesses and issuing a warning.

Residents of Lindenhofstraße were woken up around 1:50 AM by the loud bang. The quickly arriving emergency services were met with a scene of devastation. The machine was completely destroyed by the detonation, and coins and cigarette packs lay in the vicinity. The crime scene was secured and examined by ordnance disposal experts. The police are investigating for causing an explosive detonation.

In addition to criminal prosecution, the police warn: Whoever uses illegal firecrackers or makes them themselves puts themselves in great danger. Because with homemade fireworks, even the slightest thermal or mechanical influences can, under certain circumstances, lead to an explosion. Acoustic trauma, burns, mutilated or severed body parts, and other severe injuries, up to and including death – these can be the consequences of improper use of illegal, homemade firecrackers.

title_en: Cigarette machine blown up in Gröpelingen
description_en:
Unknown individuals blew up a cigarette machine in Gröpelingen in the early hours of Wednesday morning. The police are looking for witnesses and issuing a warning.

At 00:10, residents on Seewenjestraße heard a loud bang. When they looked onto the street, they saw two men tampering with the cigarette machine. The perpetrators had blown up the machine and stolen cigarette packs. The explosion significantly damaged the machine. The unknown individuals fled in the direction of the street "In den Barken".

The duo was described as follows: They are said to be approximately 20 years old, both wore black clothing and a thick winter jacket. In addition, one wore a hat and had a dark beard.

Bremen police are now investigating for causing an explosive detonation.

As early as Friday (see press release no. 0478), many people were out and about again at the Schlachte and in the Viertel on Saturday evening and during the night. The police were again deployed in increased numbers and checked compliance with the Corona rules. In addition, extra police officers monitored the driving ban at the Sielwall crossing.

The good weather again led to a high volume of people at the Schlachte. The outdoor gastronomy there was completely booked. With a peaceful and exuberant atmosphere, visitors adhered to the Corona regulations. There were no noteworthy incidents.

At the Osterdeich, there were approximately 1600 people at peak times, who initially gathered peacefully in many small groups. The police again used loudspeaker announcements to point out the hygiene rules as well as the alcohol consumption ban and carrying ban from 1 a.m. onwards. In addition, they again illuminated areas on the Osterdeich during the night. As time progressed and alcohol consumption increased, the aggressiveness of some visitors in the Viertel rose. For example, a 17-year-old initially insulted the emergency services near the ferry landing and then resisted the measures. He was taken to a police station and picked up there by his mother. The emergency services filed further criminal charges after brawls and violations of the Narcotics Act. In addition, a total of 20 administrative offenses were registered, where people did not adhere to the ban on carrying and consuming alcohol.

From 9 p.m., the police consistently enforced the driving ban at the Sielwall crossing. Police officers turned away unauthorized drivers at specially set up checkpoints. Due to many vehicles turning around, critical traffic situations sometimes arose. In addition, traffic sometimes jammed and some drivers diverted into adjacent side streets. In Schmidtstraße, unknown persons stretched barrier tape across the roadway. Alerted emergency services removed it. In the meantime, several people gathered on the roadway at the Sielwall crossing. Police officers sent the pedestrians back to the sidewalk. In addition, the officers spoke to several visitors with excessively loud music boxes. One box was confiscated after repeated noise pollution.

title_en: A night on duty in Bremen
description_en:
The good weather again led to a high volume of people in the Hanseatic city on the night from Friday to Saturday. The police again had their hands full.

In warm temperatures, numerous people took the opportunity to meet outdoors or to take advantage of the reopened gastronomic offerings. At the popular locations Schlachte, Viertel, and Osterdeich, the police forces deployed with a focus on these areas observed numerous violations of the still-existing provisions of the Corona Ordinance. Particularly the obligation to wear a mouth-nose covering in frequented places was largely ignored. In the Viertel alone, police officers registered almost 100 disregardings within half an hour. The public order office and police punished the violations accordingly. Some gastronomic establishments in the Viertel violated the prescribed closing times; charges were also filed in these cases.

Primarily young people celebrated with their music speakers on the Osterdeich meadows and on the streets and sidewalks around Sielwalleck, without, however, obstructing traffic. With increasing alcohol consumption, the potential for aggression rose in some cases, and police intervention became necessary due to altercations. This involved insults to the emergency forces and isolated bottle throws against patrol cars. Speeders and posers were also observed, particularly in the city center, Steintor, and Ostertor areas; offenses were punished accordingly. Around 1:20 AM, plainclothes officers observed an escalating altercation between about 20 people on the Osterdeich. A 24-year-old participant threatened his opponent with a knife. The 24-year-old did not comply with the demand to drop the knife. Only when a police officer drew his weapon did he allow himself to be arrested and was taken to the station.

The rubbish left behind and broken glass bottles necessitated an unscheduled cleaning by Bremen's waste management companies at the end of the night.

The police continue to appeal: Even if the Corona situation is slowly relaxing, please act with reason and insight in the coming weeks. Adhere to the measures, even if it is difficult.

In Bremen, an amendment to the general decree on additional openings and relaxations was decided and published with the 26th Corona Ordinance (§ 22b para. 1). Among other things, the changes uniformly shift the closing time for gastronomy to 1 a.m. In addition, the public order office has extended the general decree on the prohibition of off-premise alcohol sales (10 p.m. to 6 a.m.) to include a ban on carrying and consumption. Accordingly, carrying and consuming alcoholic beverages are prohibited daily from 1 a.m. to 6 a.m. in the Schlachte area and in the Viertel. Both regulations come into force today, June 11, 2021 (areas of application see attachment). To ensure that everyone is aware of the short-term changes, police forces will be out this afternoon in the Schlachte and Viertel areas to inform people about the new regulations with flyers. As already announced, the police will be out in greater numbers this weekend (see press release no. 0438) and will also monitor compliance with the new rules. In particular, violations of the ban on carrying/consuming alcohol can become expensive from 1 a.m., as they are subject to a fine of between 300 and 2000 euros according to the current general decree. The Bremen police are counting on your insight and common sense. Due to the summer weather and the announced relaxations, young people, in particular, are currently out and about. And where many people are out, there is also increased potential for conflict. The last two weekends have shown this. Therefore: Adhere to the measures, even if it is difficult. Avoid gatherings, maintain distances, and do not visit highly frequented places. Should all appeals prove ineffective, evictions will be issued, and as a last resort, incorrigible offenders will face financial penalties.

In the night leading up to Monday, police officers from Bremen provisionally arrested a man exhibiting psychological abnormalities in Hemelingen. The 43-year-old had previously rampaged and shouted around. He subsequently threatened alerted police officers. By threatening the use of firearms and tasers, the dangerous situation could be brought under control.
At around 00:05, emergency services were called to Vahrer Straße due to a noise disturbance. On site, they encountered a man standing on the sidewalk wearing a balaclava and quartz sand gloves, exhibiting psychological abnormalities by talking to himself and making a confused impression. He reacted uncooperatively and aggressively to the officers' address. Several witnesses reported that he had previously smashed the pane of a partition on a balcony and attempted to kick in a neighbor's door. The officers tried to engage him in conversation and accompanied the 43-year-old man to his apartment. Once there, he suddenly grabbed an elongated, silver object and positioned himself threateningly towards the intervening officers. At this point, it could not be ruled out that it might be a knife. He was ordered to put the object on the floor. He did not comply. Only after the use of a firearm and a taser was threatened did the 43-year-old allow himself to be arrested without resistance. The object turned out to be an extendable baton.
The officers took the psychologically abnormal man to the station. He was subsequently taken to a psychiatric facility for assessment.

Two knife-wielding individuals triggered police operations on Wednesday in Huchting and Woltmershausen. They were overpowered by alerted emergency forces. Both individuals exhibited noticeable psychological behavior and were assessed accordingly. Around 6 PM, police were initially called to an apartment on Langlütjensand after a resident's former partner had forcibly gained entry. When the emergency forces arrived, he menacingly took possession of a long kitchen knife. At this point, the caller and her children had already fled into an adjoining room and locked themselves in. Since the intruder did not react to the instruction to drop the knife, the police threatened to use firearms. Only then did the 30-year-old drop the knife. The man was restrained on the ground and handcuffed. He was handed over to the socio-psychiatric service for assessment. Late in the evening, emergency forces then moved out for an operation in Woltmershausen. There, an intoxicated couple had gotten into a loud argument in an apartment on Woltmershauser Straße. The altercation finally escalated to such an extent that the woman repeatedly attacked her partner with a knife, injuring his hand. When the police arrived, the emergency forces first had to deploy tear gas and threaten to use firearms until the 46-year-old threw away the knife. She subsequently allowed herself to be arrested without resistance. She and her 39-year-old boyfriend were treated on-site by paramedics for minor injuries. Subsequently, the woman was placed in a psychiatric facility. Further investigations are ongoing.

On Monday morning, there was a fire at the Bremen climate camp. The fire was quickly extinguished. Nobody was injured. A 21-year-old suspect was apprehended after a short escape. Witnesses observed a woman setting fire to wood remains at the climate camp in the Wallanlagen during the morning. Upon the arrival of the first police forces, she fled but was apprehended a short time later. The fire department was able to extinguish the fire quickly. There were no people left in the camp. The 21-year-old, who exhibited unusual behavior, resisted arrest and further police measures. With the help of support forces, she was restrained and presented at a police station. In her backpack, officers found, among other things, a one-handed knife, a push dagger, and pepper spray. The items were confiscated. After a medical evaluation, she was admitted to a psychiatric facility. Investigations are ongoing.

Traffic experts from the Bremen police checked motorhomes and caravans on the motorway on Saturday. Several overloading violations were identified and rectified on site. Incorrect loading and overloading affect the driving characteristics and braking behavior of motorhomes and caravans. Traffic safety for oneself and others is then no longer guaranteed. For this reason, the specialists from traffic enforcement checked 15 vehicles on the A1 in Hemelingen. Water proved to be the main problem during the checks. Most drivers were traveling on holiday with full water tanks. Overloads were found in five of the checked vehicles, which could usually be remedied by draining fresh water. In two cases, violations of load securing regulations were found. A driver of a caravan combination had to transfer part of his load from the caravan to his towing vehicle to be able to continue his journey. Many were surprised by the overloading of their caravans. The police therefore advise all motorhome drivers: Pay attention to the weight of your vehicle before you even start driving. Even the subsequent installation of additional equipment such as televisions or maneuvering aids can lead to serious changes.

Emergency services from the Bremen police and six other federal states, customs, and various other authorities and organizations with security responsibilities conducted a large-scale inspection with a focus on waste and hazardous materials in Europaallee on Wednesday. A total of 60 trucks were inspected. Several violations were identified.

Between 10 AM and 5 PM, the emergency services in Hemelingen inspected a total of 60 trucks. The vehicles were checked for waste and hazardous material loads and their technical condition. In addition, the drivers were also checked for alcohol and drug consumption. Across the respective areas, a total of 17 defects and 26 administrative offenses were identified. The police also filed two criminal charges and identified two further violations of accident prevention regulations.

The police warn: The transportation of hazardous goods, in addition to the existing general risk of accidents in road traffic, poses an additional danger. Accidents involving trucks transporting hazardous materials often lead to severe consequences for road users and the environment. Compliance with safety regulations for transporters is therefore of particular importance.

title_en: Large-scale inspection Waste and Dangerous Goods
description_en:
On Wednesday, emergency services from the police in Bremen, Hamburg, Bremerhaven, customs, and employees of the waste management authority carried out a major inspection in Europaallee, focusing on waste and dangerous goods. The transport of dangerous goods poses an additional risk in road traffic, beyond the already existing general accident risk. Accidents involving trucks transporting dangerous goods often lead to severe consequences for road users and the environment.

Between 10:00 AM and 5:00 PM, the emergency services inspected a total of 56 trucks. During this time, the trucks were specifically checked for the loading of waste and dangerous goods and their technical condition, as well as the drivers for alcohol and drug consumption.

14 violations were identified in the dangerous goods sector, 20 in the waste sector, and two deficiencies in the technical condition. Corresponding administrative offenses and warnings will be issued by the police and the responsible waste management authority.

Bremen Police will continue to carry out targeted inspections in the future.

title_en: Suspicious package in the town hall, suspicious letter at the FDP
description_en: A suspicious package in Bremen City Hall and a suspicious letter at the FDP triggered major operations by the fire department and police in the city center on Tuesday morning. The package was delivered by mail. The employees in the City Hall building were initially evacuated as a precautionary measure. The package was examined by specialists from the Federal Police and the fire department; the contents were harmless. A suspicious letter containing a powdery substance was discovered in the mailbox of the FDP's state office in the morning. Here too, the examination revealed that the contents were a non-hazardous substance. The State Security Department of the Bremen Police has launched investigations in both cases. The Special Commission "Spielplatz" is also investigating whether there is a connection to previous mailings.

The investigators of the "Spielplatz" (Playground) Special Commission were able to attribute with high probability a knife found on a playground in Neustadt and a powder letter sent to the Green Party to the perpetrator who had repeatedly been active in the past with these modus operandi. By publishing a handwriting sample and a picture of the knife, the police hope for further information from the public.

On Monday, July 6, a powder letter was received at the office of the party Bündnis 90 / Die Grünen (Alliance 90 / The Greens) and on a playground at Niedersachsendamm, an employee of a family center found a so-called utility knife. The knife lay on the ground in the sand between a container and the play equipment. According to current findings of the Soko Spielplatz, the perpetrator in the three cases of knives deposited on playgrounds is very probably the same man who has sent a total of 34 powder letters since early January. With his actions, he presumably wants to terrorize the public and generate attention. The geographical proximity of the crime scenes also suggests a connection between the acts.

In recent months, various political parties in Bremen and Lower Saxony received diverse letters with powdery additions and partly anti-constitutional content. The letters were mostly handwritten.

The police are now publishing the perpetrator's handwriting and a photo of the found knife and ask:

A suspicious letter in an office of the Bündnis90/The Greens party triggered a major deployment of police and fire services on Monday midday in Bremen city centre. An employee of the office on Altenwall street noticed a powdery substance in a letter and alerted the police. The letter was examined by specialists from the Federal Police and the fire department. The examination revealed that it was a non-hazardous substance. The criminal police have launched an investigation.

In the Bremen districts of Walle and Hemelingen, a trans woman and a man of Russian origin were slightly injured by unknown assailants on Friday afternoon. The police are looking for witnesses. The 40-year-old was walking her dog and two goats on Waller Straße and was initially lightly touched by a passing car, according to her own statement. The driver then got out and, for reasons not yet clarified, uttered insults and threats. The 40-year-old continued her way through a green area and met the driver again on the street "Auf den Barken," who was now accompanied by two young men. According to her own statements, the trans woman was spat at, hit, and grabbed on the breast by the trio. After the driver sprayed her with pepper spray, the attackers fled in the car or on two e-scooters. The 40-year-old Bremen resident was treated on site by paramedics. The driver was described as corpulent, with dark complexion and short black hair. He fled in a black VW. Around 4:10 PM, a 35-year-old Bremen resident was asked by four men on the parking lot of a car repair shop on Hastedter Heerstraße if he was Russian. After he affirmed this, the individuals identified themselves as Ukrainians and one of the men punched him in the face, causing the 35-year-old to fall to the ground. After another from the group also physically attacked him, the Bremen resident fled to a nearby bus stop. The attackers were described as being around 40 years old and wearing dark work clothes.

In Bremen's Neustadt district, a 57-year-old trans woman was insulted by a group of youths on Saturday evening and subsequently severely injured. The youths fled undetected after the act. The police are looking for witnesses.The woman from Bremen was traveling on tram line 4 towards Neustadt around 7:35 PM when several youths boarded at the Domsheide stop. The group, consisting of almost 15 people, immediately insulted the 57-year-old as a "fucking tranny" and ripped her wig off her head. Subsequently, she was repeatedly punched in the face with both fists by one of the youths. His companions loudly cheered on the attacker. Only when other passengers intervened to help did they stop assaulting the woman. The group of perpetrators left the tram at the Schwankhalle stop and fled in an unknown direction. The 57-year-old had to be taken to a hospital with severe facial injuries.The youth who attacked the woman with his fists is said to be between 14 and 16 years old and approximately 1.70 meters tall, with brown hair. At the time of the incident, he was wearing a white T-shirt and a shoulder bag.

A 25-year-old beat up two young women in a tram in the station district on Friday evening. The trigger for the attack is said to have been the women's sexual orientation. Responding officers were able to apprehend the suspect still at the scene.

The two 18 and 19-year-old women had boarded the Line 8 tram at the Haferkamp stop and were traveling towards the main train station. When the two kissed, the 25-year-old approached them and insulted them with queerphobic remarks. This led to an altercation, during which the man suddenly punched the women in the face with his fist. When the 18-year-old then fell unconscious to the ground, the attacker kicked her in the stomach with his foot. Both had to be taken to the hospital for outpatient treatment.

Officers from the Taskforce, which was primarily deployed in the station area, noticed the incident, stopped the tram, and apprehended the suspect. The 25-year-old man from Romania was taken to the police station for further measures. The criminal police are now investigating him for aggravated assault. The State Security, which is responsible for cases of hate crime, has taken over the further investigations.

Following several money laundering offenses, the public prosecutor's office and the Bremen police are searching for a previously unknown perpetrator with a photograph. In 2025, the man opened a bank account under a false identity using a stolen identity card. For this purpose, the address sticker on the ID card was forged and the alleged registration address was inserted. Subsequently, funds totaling a five-figure sum from other fraudulent offenses were received using this account. A picture of the money launderer was taken when the bank account was opened. Extensive investigations have not yet led to the identification of the man. The Bremen police and public prosecutor's office are now searching for him with a photograph.

title_en: Public search for a female money launderer
description_en: Following several money laundering offenses, the public prosecutor's office and the Bremen police are searching with a photo for a previously unknown female perpetrator. In 2021, the woman opened a bank account under a false identity using a falsified South African identity card. Subsequently, funds in the total five-figure range from other fraudulent crimes were received using this account. A picture of the woman was taken during the opening of the bank accounts. However, extensive investigations have not yet led to her identification. The Bremen police and public prosecutor's office are now searching for her with a photo. The police are asking the public for assistance and ask: Who can provide information about the person pictured?

The Public Prosecutor's Office and the Bremen Police are searching for an account fraudster using photographs. The previously unknown perpetrator opened an account at a bank in summer 2023 with a stolen ID card, onto which larger sums of money from other criminal offenses were deposited and subsequently transferred. As previous investigations did not lead to the identification of the perpetrator, the Police and Public Prosecutor's Office are searching for him using two images and ask: "Who can provide information about the man in the photo, who knows him?"

On Wednesday evening, a witness reported to the police that she had observed a woman being dragged into a van in Farge. The police are looking for witnesses. Numerous rumors are already circulating on social networks. It is requested not to spread these, but only to share verified information from the police.The allegedly missing person is said to be in her early 20s and have hip-length, blonde hair. She was wearing dark winter boots, a long white coat, and a black hat. She was accompanied by a small, white dog, presumably of the Shih Tzu breed. The incident is said to have occurred around 5:30 PM in the Berner Fährweg/Witteborg area. The relevant vehicle is described as a white van with possibly foreign license plates.The Bremen police are working at full speed on the investigation, but so far no verified information is available, so the facts of the matter cannot currently be confirmed. The police are looking for witnesses and ask: "Who made suspicious observations at the location?" Should someone recognize themselves in the description, this person is also urgently requested to contact the police.

Since Sunday noon, 74-year-old Jürgen Hans Hermann Grau from Arbergen has been missing. He had not returned home after a short walk. Mr. Grau left his home address on Sunday around 11:30 AM and has not been seen since. The missing person is demented and disoriented. He is 1.70 meters tall, stocky, and walks with a forward stoop. He has white, short hair. At the time of his disappearance, Mr. Grau was dressed in a beige winter jacket, jeans, and black shoes. Extensive search efforts, including with Mantrailer dogs and a helicopter, have so far not led to finding the missing person.

Bremen Police had asked for help in mid-March with the search for 56-year-old Daniel Franz from Oslebshausen. Mr. Franz suffers from a mental illness and is dependent on medication. Due to his state of health, it could not be ruled out that he was in a helpless situation.Mr. Franz has now been located. There are no indications of a criminal offense.Bremen Police ask that the search and the published photo be deleted.

A 15-year-old drowned on Monday in Lake Achterdiek in Oberneuland. Bremen police have commenced investigations into the cause of death. The teenager was swimming in the lake and suddenly could no longer stay above the water's surface. Helpers tried in vain to rescue him from the water. Several bathers then searched for him. A witness finally discovered the 15-year-old, and fire department divers pulled him out of the water. Resuscitation attempts were unsuccessful. Further investigations are ongoing. Approximately 150 to 200 onlookers initially blocked the path of the rescue and emergency services. During the resuscitation, helpers and bathers initially shielded these measures with towels and blankets. This led to obstructions caused by onlookers who took photos and videos with their mobile phones. The police first had to set up privacy screens and cordon off the rescue site to get the surrounding people to leave. The police emphatically point out: If you are not a witness or providing first aid, please do not stay unnecessarily long at accident scenes and do not hinder the work of emergency and rescue services.

On the night from Saturday to Sunday, a 27-year-old drowned in Werdersee. Extensive search and rescue measures remained unsuccessful.

The young man was with friends near the DLRG station at the local swimming beach. When a volleyball fell into the lake, he went into the water and sank approximately 20 meters from the shore below the waterline. An extensive search by witnesses, police, DLRG, and fire department was carried out. Rescue divers and swimmers as well as a boat with sonar equipment were deployed. The man from Afghanistan was recovered lifeless some time later; resuscitation attempts remained unsuccessful.

Witnesses to the incident were cared for on site by police and rescue personnel; the friends of the deceased were taken to a hospital for counseling and support. The criminal police investigation into the cause of death is ongoing.

On Tuesday morning, a male body was discovered in the Weser. Bremen police currently assume that it is the missing 18-year-old who had attempted to swim across the river over the weekend (see press release 0462). On Friday night/early Saturday morning, the 18-year-old, together with an acquaintance, had attempted to swim across the Weser approximately at the level of Sielwall. He did not subsequently return to the bank. Extensive search efforts remained unsuccessful. The identification of the body is not yet fully complete; however, after consulting with the relatives, Bremen police assume that it is the 18-year-old. There are currently no indications of foul play.

title_en: Shots in Neustadt - Police and public prosecutor's office investigate
description_en:
On Saturday evening, a 25-year-old man was seriously injured by gunshots in Bremen's Neustadt district (see press release no. 0215). The public prosecutor's office and the police are investigating a suspected attempted murder.
Around 8 PM, witnesses reported gunshots via the police emergency number at the corner of Gastfeldstraße and Meyerstraße. Quickly arriving Bremen police officers found a 25-year-old injured man at the scene. He sustained multiple gunshot wounds to his legs. The officers immediately provided first aid, including applying so-called tourniquets. The man was taken to a hospital where he underwent surgery. There is no danger to his life. Emergency services cordoned off the area, secured evidence, and questioned witnesses. An extensive manhunt initially remained unsuccessful.
The public prosecutor's office and the Bremen police are now investigating a suspected attempted murder. Additionally, it is being investigated whether there are connections to the crime of March 17, 2026 (press release no. 0189).

On Sunday afternoon, emergency services of the Bremen police found a 42-year-old injured man in the Neustadt district. Previously, callers had reported shots via the emergency number. As a result, a large-scale police operation was triggered. At approximately 12:00 PM, several callers reported shots in Nollendorfer Straße via the police emergency number. Shortly thereafter, emergency services were on site in large numbers and secured the area. They found a 42-year-old man with a gunshot wound and immediately provided first aid. He was taken to a hospital with a gunshot wound to the leg; at times, his life was in danger. Agitated relatives of the man had to be calmed down on site by a strong police presence. There are currently no further injured persons. Subsequently, the police initiated extensive search operations for possible perpetrators: emergency services questioned witnesses, forensic investigators were on site, and police dogs were also deployed. Witnesses stated that they had previously seen a man armed with a firearm. The investigations are currently ongoing, and the Bremen police currently assume that the 42-year-old and the perpetrator knew each other.

title_en: Police release wanted photo after shooting in Woltmershausen
description_en: After a 40-year-old man was shot in the Woltmershausen district of Bremen in August (see also press release 552), the police were able to identify the suspected perpetrator and are searching for the 29-year-old with a photo. For reasons not yet fully clarified, the 40-year-old and his brother got into an argument in Dangaster Straße with two men aged 28 and 29. The 29-year-old is then said to have shot the man from Bremen in the course of events. Subsequently, the duo fled. Extensive search and investigation measures by the police followed. In addition, important evidence could be found, seized and examined. The results of this intensive work led to the suspected shooter Mahsum Demir.

title_en: Money launderer turns herself in to the police
description_en: The public prosecutor's office and the Bremen police were searching for a money launderer with a public wanted notice; see also press release 0597. The 24-year-old turned herself in to the police on Wednesday. Last year, the woman opened accounts under a false identity using a stolen ID card. Subsequently, funds totaling a five-figure sum from other fraudulent activities were received using these fraudulently obtained accounts. The 24-year-old fraudster turned herself in due to the pressure of the search and admitted to the crimes. Further investigations are ongoing. The search from press release 0597 is thus concluded, and the images are to be deleted accordingly.

title_en: Investigative Success: Female money launderer turns herself in to the police
description_en: The public prosecutor's office and the Bremen police were searching for a money launderer with a public appeal; see also press release 0741. In 2023, the money launderer opened accounts at various banks using several false identities. In total, funds from criminal offenses in the six-figure range were transferred via these accounts. The police and public prosecutor's office then searched for the perpetrator using a photo, which has now led to success: The woman has now reported to the police via a lawyer and surrendered. Further investigations are ongoing. The search from press release 0741 has therefore been concluded, and the images are to be deleted accordingly.

The public prosecutor's office and the Bremen police were searching for a suspected fraudster with a public appeal, see also press release 0255. A 19-year-old from Bremen has now been identified. Unknown individuals had called an 85-year-old woman at the beginning of December 2022 and pretended to be bank employees. As a result, the perpetrators obtained the senior citizen's PIN number and EC card. Later, a man withdrew money in a branch. The police and public prosecutor's office subsequently searched for him with pictures, which has now led to success: Several witnesses recognized the 19-year-old from Bremen and notified the permanent criminal investigation service. Further investigations are ongoing. The search from press release 0255 is thus concluded, and the images are to be deleted accordingly.

On the night from Monday to Tuesday, a violent attack occurred in Bremen-Mitte. A 35-year-old was slightly injured, and the 22-year-old attacker could be identified and apprehended thanks to witness statements and video recordings. Shortly after 2:00 AM, two men got into an argument in the main hall of the central train station. In front of witnesses, one of the men stood up and kicked his opponent, who was sitting opposite him, in the face with his foot. The perpetrator then repeatedly struck the 35-year-old's head with a metallic pipe tamper in his fist, while the victim protected his face with his hands. With lacerations to his face and suspected concussion, he had to be treated as an outpatient in a hospital. The 22-year-old fled the scene. Through witness statements and video surveillance in the station, both the act could be observed and the assailant apprehended a short time later. State and federal police worked hand in hand during this operation. As the injured man could have lost his eyesight due to the nature of the attack, the police are now investigating on suspicion of attempted grievous bodily harm and grievous bodily harm. The Bremen police also point out that any kick to a person's head can be fatal; a few centimeters can make the difference. It regularly depends solely on chance whether life-threatening injuries are caused by such kicks. The Bremen police pursue these offenses with full consequence.

title_en: Arrests after kicks to the head
description_en:
In the night leading into Monday, two young men in the Neustadt district beat and kicked a 26-year-old and then fled. Police officers located the two a short time later near the train station and arrested them.

Witnesses had noticed a loud altercation between three men on Langemarckstraße around 02:40 AM. This developed into a fight during which the 26-year-old was knocked to the ground by the two 19 and 26-year-old men. According to witness statements, they reportedly repeatedly continued to punch and kick the person lying on the ground. After that, they fled. The 26-year-old had to be admitted to a hospital with serious injuries for inpatient treatment. The alerted police officers immediately initiated search measures and located the two men near Bremen Central Station and arrested them. They are being investigated on suspicion of attempted manslaughter. The examination of the grounds for detention is currently ongoing.

Every kick to a person's head can be fatal; a few centimeters can make all the difference. It regularly depends solely on chance whether life-threatening injuries are caused by the kicks. The Bremen police pursue these offenses with utmost determination.

title_en: 35-year-old in custody after kicks to the head
description_en:
On Sunday night, several men in Farge beat and kicked a 21-year-old, seriously injuring him. Kicks to the head are also said to have occurred. Police officers located four suspects in a residential building a short time later and arrested them. An arrest warrant was issued against a 35-year-old.

Around 00:20 AM, witnesses reported an altercation in Richard-Taylor-Straße, during which the 21-year-old was suddenly knocked to the ground by several men. According to witness statements, they continued to beat and kick the person lying on the ground, including kicks to the head. The attackers only stopped and fled when patrol cars arrived. The 21-year-old had to be treated for serious injuries in a hospital. The alerted police officers immediately initiated search operations and located four suspects in an apartment, arresting them. The four men, aged 27, 35, and 39, are being investigated on suspicion of attempted manslaughter. A judge, at the request of the Bremen public prosecutor's office, issued an arrest warrant against a 35-year-old. All parties involved knew each other; the motives for the crime are currently unclear.

Every kick to a person's head can be fatal; a few centimeters can make the difference. It regularly depends solely on chance whether the kicks cause life-threatening injuries. The Bremen police pursue these offenses with full consequence.

On Tuesday evening, a 27-year-old threw stones into a car dealership in the Hastedt district. When emergency services attempted to arrest him, he resisted massively. A short time later, in the Steintor district, a 25-year-old resisted arrest. The man was taken into custody.

Around 5:40 PM, two witnesses saw the 27-year-old man throwing stones into a car dealership on Stresemannstraße. One filmed the incident with his smartphone, the other called 110. Alerted emergency services found the man at a bus stop. When the police officers attempted to search him, he resisted massively and repeatedly spat and kicked in the direction of the emergency services. A spit hood had to be placed on him. In the patrol car, he continued to behave aggressively, continuing to kick and spit. Police officers took him to the station. The 27-year-old man now faces criminal charges for property damage, assault, resisting arrest, and assault on law enforcement officers.

A short time later, around 11:30 PM, police officers issued a 25-year-old in Wielandstraße with an order to leave the premises. Previously, his girlfriend had issued him a house ban because he allegedly beat her and had not left the apartment despite being asked. When he reappeared a short time later in the hallway of the apartment building, alerted emergency services arrived. He did not react to the police officers' address, whereupon they took him into custody. During the arrest, he grabbed a police officer's genital area. Using force, the police officer was able to free himself and restrain the 25-year-old on the ground and arrest him. The man now faces a criminal charge for resisting law enforcement officers.

During operations in Vegesack and Mitte on Thursday, two individuals offered significant resistance to emergency personnel. One police officer was slightly injured.

Initially, at approximately 12:45 PM, a man was reported to the police who was allegedly attempting to smash windowpanes with a manhole cover on Kirchheide street. On arrival, emergency personnel encountered a 39-year-old man who was identified by witnesses as the suspect. He initially did not respond to being addressed and subsequently lost control, lashed out, and offered considerable resistance during his arrest. He was eventually brought to the ground and continued to resist significantly there. He was taken to the police station; prior to that, he had stated he had consumed crack. A criminal complaint for assault and resisting law enforcement officers was filed. A police officer sustained minor hand injuries.

At approximately 4:20 PM, emergency personnel were called to Domsheide due to an assault. There, a 23-year-old initially presented himself as the victim. Witnesses stated that he had previously massively insulted a couple and was subsequently hit by a 26-year-old. In the course of recording the facts and clarifying the situation, he became increasingly aggressive, screamed around, and insulted passers-by. Even after repeated attempts to address him, he could not be calmed down and eventually tried to flee. When the emergency personnel held him, he offered massive resistance and continued to scream. He was eventually taken to the police station and criminal complaints, including for resisting law enforcement officers, were filed. In both cases, further investigations are ongoing.

On the night of Saturday to Sunday, a 24-year-old in Mitte fled from emergency services who wanted to clarify a matter in front of a disco on Rembertiring. The man ran in the direction of Contrescarpe, jumped into the city moat, and tried to swim to the other bank. Approximately halfway, he lost control, submerged, and panicked. He shouted that he couldn't swim and was threatening to drown. The pursuing police officers didn't hesitate for a second and also jumped into the cold water to rescue the man. They brought him safely to the other bank. Subsequently, the 24-year-old was taken to the hospital and admitted for inpatient care. During a search of the man, police officers found several sales units of cocaine. Further investigations are ongoing.

On Tuesday afternoon, a 55-year-old pedestrian in Vahr had his gold necklace stolen by an unknown assailant using a trick while on his way to work. At approximately 1:03 PM, the man who was later robbed was approached by an approximately 30-year-old man unknown to him, who had apparently previously been riding along with another man on an electric scooter. This man asked him for a cigarette and then hugged him so effusively that he lightly scratched him on the neck. He then went back to the e-scooter rider and rode away with him. Only a few minutes later, at his workplace, the 55-year-old noticed the absence of his golden necklace, worth several thousand euros. The perpetrator could only be roughly described as having black hair, wearing black sportswear, and being approximately 175-180 cm tall.

title_en: Gold chains stolen from jewelry store
description_en: On Friday afternoon, an unknown man stole valuable gold chains from a jewelry store in Bremen's Old Town. The police are looking for witnesses and warn against buying the chains. Around 3:50 PM, the perpetrator entered the jewelry store on Pelzerstraße and walked directly towards a display case. With an emergency hammer, he immediately smashed the glass, grabbed four golden necklaces from the display, and ran out of the store in the direction of Knochenhauerstraße. The thief is said to be approximately 1.80 meters tall. He was wearing a black hooded jacket, red jogging pants with white stripes, a black cap with a gold emblem, and grey sneakers.

In Bremen, handbags have been increasingly stolen from bicycle baskets in recent weeks. The police are investigating and giving important tips. On Monday afternoon, an 85-year-old woman from Bremen filed a criminal complaint for theft at the Schwachhausen police station. According to her own statements, the senior citizen was pushing her bicycle up the ramp at Bischofsnadel on Sunday and unexpectedly received assistance from a young man. Shortly afterwards, she discovered that the unknown helper had stolen her wallet from her handbag, which was located in the bicycle basket on the luggage rack. Bremen police have registered an increased number of cases in recent weeks where thieves snatched handbags and other valuables from bicycle baskets. Investigations into these matters are ongoing. The police recommend:

A burglar broke into a ground-floor apartment in Findorff through a tilted window early on Monday morning. When the tenant surprised him, the man pushed her aside and fled with the loot.
The burglar entered the house on Herbststraße through the window and searched the apartment for valuables. The 65-year-old tenant was sitting on the terrace, became aware of noises, and went inside. In the bedroom, she encountered the intruder, who immediately grabbed the senior by her arms and pushed her aside. He snatched her smartphone from her hand, pocketed her wallet, and fled by bicycle towards Bürgerweide. The 65-year-old suffered minor injuries due to the attack.
The robber was described as approximately 30 years old, 170 centimeters tall, slim, with short black hair. He was wearing dark clothing.

title_en: 23 cats, two boxes and many questions
description_en: On Wednesday morning, the Bremen police were called to an unusual incident in Marschstraße in the Hemelingen district. An attentive citizen had discovered two cardboard boxes at the entrance of a cemetery, from which soft meowing emanated. On site, the suspicion was confirmed: The cardboard boxes, sealed with packing tape and provided with only a few air holes, contained a total of 23 cats - including three adult animals and 20 newborn kittens. The insides of the boxes were already soaked with urine; one box also contained some cat food. When the boxes were carefully opened, a suspected mother cat took the opportunity to escape. The remaining 22 cats were secured by the emergency services, transported to the police station, and given initial care there. Subsequently, the animals - including food rations donated in the meantime by helpful citizens - were handed over to the Bremen animal shelter. A check of the adult animals using a chip reader yielded no results. There are currently no leads regarding the previously unknown perpetrators.

title_en: Swan killed at Werdersee - Police seek witnesses
description_en:
On Wednesday afternoon, a walker discovered a killed swan at the Werdersee lake in Neustadt, whose head along with its neck had been severed. The Bremen police are asking for information.

The animal lay on the side of Werderinsel in a green strip between the cycling and pedestrian path, near the shore. Emergency services found the swan on site and searched the immediate vicinity for further carcasses or injured animals - without any further findings.

The police and the animal welfare authority are investigating due to a criminal offense under the Animal Welfare Act. This provides for such acts a prison sentence of up to three years or a fine.
